1.1. Origin of Rahu/Ketu Rules 


(KP Reader ||, 1983, page 315 ) 


Rahu or Ketu will act as a strong agent to the planets to which they are conjoined. |f they are not conjoined 
with any planet, then they give the results of the planet which aspects them. Only when they are neither 
conjoined with, nor aspected by any planet, they represent the lord of the house. (Uthrakalamrita -- Khanda VI 
Sloka 14 onwards) 


1.2. Rahu/Ketu Rules by Guruji KSK 

(KP Reader || 1, Old Edition/OE/, Part 1, page 123/New Edition/NE/ page 130; KP Reader V, 1983, page 123) 
1) Rahu or Kethu indicates the results of planet which it is conjoined; 

2) 1f no planet in conjunction, the results of planets aspecting it; 


3) |f neither conjoined nor aspected, the results of the constellation in which it is deposited; 
4) Lastly the result of the signin which it is deposited. 


1.3. Similar Version by Sri C. B. Bhatt 

(Nakshatra Chintamani, page 19) 

Rahu/ Ketu as PLANET gives: 

1) Firstly, the results of the planet in conjunction with it, 
2) Secondly, the results of the planet aspecting It, 


3) Thirdly, the results of its own star lord, and 
4) Fourthly, the results of the owner of the sign occupied by it. 


1.4. A Slightly Different Version by Guruji KSK 


(by taking the STARLORD "before" the planet in aspect/ KP Reader VI, 1978/2002, pages 
187/212/214/274/ 276) 


A node gives: 

1) Firstly, the result of the planet or planets with which it is conjoined, 
2) Secondly, of the star lord in which it is deposited, 

3) Then, of the planet or planets aspecting it and 

4) Lastly, of the lord of the sign in which it is deposited. 


ll. HOUSE OCCUPIED BY RAHU/KETU 


(KP Reader || 1, OE, Part 1, page 124 /NE, page 130/ KP Reader V, 1983, page 124) 


2.1. The Role of House Occupied by Rahu/Ketu 


1) Rahu or Kethu gives results to greater extent than what Starlord can offer. 
2) | magine as though Starlord is posited in that house in which Rahu or Ketu tenanted. 
3) Also imagine that Starlord is posited inthat bhava. And it gives results to greater extent. 


2.2. KP Reader II1I|, OE, Part 1, page 110/ NE, page 116/ KP Reader V, 1983, page 110 


Rahu and Ketu will occupy a house. They govern the stars Arudhra, Swathi, Sathabisha, Aswini, Maka and Moola. 
So planets situated in these stars will offer the results as indicated by either Rahu or Kethu according to the 
house occupied by them. Further one should include the results of the lord of the constellation and then the 
lord of the sign in which Rahu and Kethu Is posited. It is explained in the end of the chapter (i.e. as furnished in 
1.2 and 2.1). 


lll.A DIFFERENT APPROACH FOR RAHU/KETU AS STARLORD 


3.1. Nakshatra Chintamani, page 19 (Sri C. B. Bhatt) 


If any planet is inthe STAR of Rahu or Ketu, 


1) that planet will signify the matters of the house occupied by Rahu or Ketu; 

2) that planet will indicate the matters of the house owned and occupied by the Star lord of Rahu or Ketu; and 
3) that planet will denote the matters of the house occupied and owned by the owner of the sign occupied by 
Rahu or Ketu. 


3.2. It is similar to 2.2 including the house occupied and excluding the planets in conjunction and aspect. 


3.3. The results of planets in conjunction and aspect for Rahu/Ketu as STARLORD is rarely applied in KP 
Readers as furnished in 1.2 and 2.2. of the Appendix. 


3.4. |t may be a little awkward in preparing a KP planet wise and star wise significator table while taking 
the starlord effects of Rahu/Ketu as STARLORD. 


IV. OTHER VIEWS 


4.1. An interesting approach is noted in Astrosecrets & KP, Part 1, 2003, page 308 and 311 (Sri M.-P. 
Shanmughan) and in KP Year Book 2002, page 40 (N. Pandu/N. Santhanalingam), that Rahu/ Ketu will offer the 
results of a planet which is deposited in Rahu/ Ketu star, eg. if Mars is deposited in Rahu star, Rahu will offer 
the results of houses 3 andl0 owned by Mars. And then the results of planets in conjunction and aspect and 
Starlord are mentioned to be considered. 


4.2. Inthe 4 Step Method (invented by Sri Sunil Gonchalekar and explained by Sri Anant Raichur in English), 
Rahu/ Ketu is taken as agent of the lord of sign occupied and as a significator of the house occupied. | f 
Rahu/ Ketu is in conjunction with any planet within 3.33 degrees, this planet is also considered, and then the 
Starlord of Rahu/Ketu, the Sublod of Rahu/Ketu, and the Starlord of the Sublord are also considered. Only 
strong significators are considered by taking into account of occupation of starlord, Rahu/ Ketu in own star, 
Rahu/ Ket having no planet in its star and empty houses. Planets in aspect are not considered unless within 3.33 
degrees. 


4.3. The importance of strong significators is emphasized in Astrology for Beginners, Vol 5, page 669 (Sri K. 
Subramanium). Only if there are no planets in Rahu/ Ketu star, Rahu/ Ket will signify the house occupied. (If a 
planet is in Rahu/Ketu star, the planet will signify the house occupied by Rahu/Ketu.) Only if there are no 
planets in the star of the signlord, Rahu/ Ketu will signify the results of the signliord. (I f a planet is in the star 
of signiord, Rahu/ Ketu will signify the houses occupied by the signiod and the starlod of the signlord and the 
houses owned by the STARLORD of the signlord, provided there is no planet in those houses). And then the 
results of the planets in conjunction and aspect are mentioned to be considered. 


V.RAHU/KETU'’S ASPECTS 


5.1. Since the Rahu/ Ketu Rules in 1.2 and 2.1 are commonly used, the application of Rahu/ Ketu’s aspects is not 
found in KP literature except Dr. Bal Krishna Singh Hatia applying Rahu s 5th and 9th aspects in KP Year Book, 
1999, page 26 and Sri Prof. K. Balachandran using Kethu's 7th, 9th and 12th (Hindu) aspects in KP Year Book, 
2002, page 82-90. According to Parasara, Rahu aspects 5, 7,9, and 12 fully (Uttara Kalamrita Kalidasa by Dr. P. 
S. Sastri, Edition 2001, page 43; Thanks to Ms. Sandy Crowther for giving reference.) and J] upiter-like aspects 
of Rahu/ Ketu are used in Vedic Astrology. 


VI.SOME FINDINGS FROM EXAMPLES IN KP READERS 


6.1. 1n examples regarding Rahu/Ketu Rules in KP Readers III, |V, V and VI (as furnishe in the Appendix), 
Hindu aspects and conjunction are used; the importance of strong significators is considered whenever 
appropriate by taking Into account of the occupation of starlord, Rahu/Ketu in own star, Rahu/Ket having no 
planet in its star and empty houses. 


6.2. Even though quoted "only when they are neither conjoined with, nor 


aspected by any planet, they represent the lord of the house." , whether Rahu/Ketu as Planet or Starlod or 
Sublord, the results of the followings are taken depending on relevance to the matter under consideration 
regardless of their sequence of order: 


1) House occupied,

Starlord,

149-50) and Reader VI pages 302/316; 

b) Conjuction/Aspect/ Signlord Rules are applied together in Reader | V page 111; 

c) Occupation/ Aspect/Signlord Rules are applied together in Reader VI, page 190; 

d) Signlord Rule is applied neglecting the planet in conjunction in Reader |I1| OE Part 2 pages 44-5/85 (NE 
pages 200-1/ 244-45). 


6.3. Rahu/Ketu as agent of the planet in conjunction or aspect or signlord is supposed to give whatever the 
planet concerned is to signify (KP Reader VI, page 234) but only houses occupied and owned by the planet are 
commonly considered, and further results of the planet's Starlord are taken in some cases only, for instances: 
1) Starlod of Starlord in Reader ||! OE Part 2 page 13 (NE page 166); 

2) Starlord of Signlord in Reader 111 OE Part 2 page 85 (NE pages 244-45), 


6.4. Generally the houses occupied and owned by STARLORD and the house occupied by Rahu/Ketu are shown 
by KP SWs, and in addition planets acted by Rahu/Ketu as agent and planets having no planet in their stars are 
also shown by KPAstro 2.5. 

VII. CONCLUSION 
In applying Rahu/Ketu Rules of house occupied, planets in conjunction and aspect, starlord and signlord, 
consideration of the priority and strong significators will be crucial when Rahu/ Ketu plays a dual role in cases of 


life or death, marriage or denial etc.

Marital discord - A KP appraisal 


Effort by 
Vijay Kumar 
Senior Manager, C-DOT, Electronic City, Phase-1 
Hosur Road, Bangalore - 560 100 
080-25119580 (Off), 26587463 (Res) 0-9845039153 (Mob) 


v kumar@cdotb.ernet.in 





Author: The author hails from the Electronics and Communication engineering background, presently 
heading a Senior Managerial position at The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), 


Bangalore. Besides teaching Parasharic and | ailmini astrology at | CAS, Bangalore and contributing to 
The Astrological Magazine in J aimini theme since a decade, the author has special interest in The 
Krishnamurti Paddhati and is a serious student of this subject. 





This case is from my file of records. 


One person contacted me to inform me about the marital discord he was undergoing and wanted me to 
analyse, if a patch up with his wife was possible? 


He gave me his birth time as 25-12-1959, 20:15 Hrs IST, Chennai for analysis. 


The birth time was corrected to 20:15:47 Hrs 1ST and analysed as follows on 17'"J an 2007. The birth 
chart is enclosed herewith. 


The chart is being analysed as follows: 
The Query 


The chart under discussion is a natal chart and the query may not be confirmed by the disposition of 
Moon or Lagna sub-lord, just as done in prashna charts. 


However, the sub-sub lord of Moon at the time of judgment may assess the state of affairs going on 
at that point of time inthe life of a querist. 


This case was taken up for analysis on 17-01-2007 at 10-13-26 Hrs 1ST at Bangalore and at that time 
J upiter ruled as sub-sub lord of Moon. J upiter in the natal chart is the 6" lord in the star of 12°" 
lord-Mercury, which was sufficient to confirm the marital discord prevailing in the life of the native. 


The co- ordinates for judgment 


In a natal /prashna chart, the harmonious life with wife is promised if Lagna, 5‘ and 7'" cusp get 
involved with the 11'" house. The marital discord starts from the 6'" house and 12'" house involving 
the 7'" house. The healthy marital life shall be realized only if the 11'" cusp indicates its linkage with 
the Lagna, 5'" and 7'" house without getting linked to the adverse houses. 


Analysis of the chart 


L, 


Look whether there is a promise for marital discord in the chart. Lagna sub-lord Moon is placed in 
the star of Rahu, which Is placed in 2H, causing disturbance in family life. The sub-lord of Moon is 
Saturn, which as 7°" and 8'" lord gets placed in 6'” house, bringing the focus of difficulties in 
married life in principle. 


Look to the 7'" sub-lord Mars that gets placed in the star of 12'" lord Mercury bringing the 
element of un-happy marital life and loss of attachment, as Mercury gets placed inthe 5'" house 
of attachment and mutual respect. 


Now, note the 11'" cusp whose sub-lord is Rahu. Rahu disposes Mercury (sign lord) and Sun (star 
lord). 2™ lord Sun is in the star of Ketu placed in 8°" indicate break of family life and Mercury in 
its own star placed in 5'" house (conjunctions not considered yet) portend the marriage to continue 
for some time, though involving discord. 


Thus, there seems to be a clear case of marital discord at some point of time in native’s life. I t is 
expected that a vulnerable dasha will trigger the marital discord. 


The native started the dasha of Mercury from Sep-2006 and as soon as he entered this dasha, 
the explosion of marital discord took place and the native was thrown out of the house. 


Note that Mercury is in its own star, hence powerful. Mercury as 3" lord indicates his point of 
view and as 12‘ lord indicates the embarrassment he has to undergo in terms of relationship. 
Since, Mercury is placed in 5'" house (the house of marital bondage by co-ordination and mutual 
felicity), the results of felicity shall get dictated by the indications of the Mercury's sub-lord and 
planetary conjunction taking place in 5‘" house involving Mercury. Lagna lord-Moon as sub-lord of 
Mercury Is placed in 

3 house, hence the native shall always be in favour of a fruitful dialogue but may not get 
benefited by this placement, as the star lord of Moon (Rahu) destroys the marital felicity (refer 
analysis of Rahu at #1). 


Now, analyse the planetary conjunctions which dasha lord - Mercury suffers in the 5°” house. 
Incidentally, Mercury gets in close conjunction with Mars (within a degree) and J upiter (within 3 
deg). Let us study it further. 


Mars is 5'" and 7'" sub-lord, thus rules marital life and felicity. Mars is very powerful planet, as no 
other planet falls in its star and Is placed in its own sign. 


Dasha lord Mercury (12'" lord) is the star lord of Mars and is closely conjunct with it, thus 
bringing the element of Martian influence in the results dispensed by Mercury, as the conjunct 
planet take over the results. Since, Mars is non-friendly to Mercury, this conjunction in the sign of 
Mars may expectedly bring the element of hot exchanges (Mars), breaking away harmony (5°? 
house) and ensuring loss of marital life (Mercury being 6'" lord from 7°" house). The sub-lord of 
Mars (Moon) would decide the end result given by Mars, which is placed in 3° house, giving an 
Opportunity to the native to deliberate on the issues. Since, Moon is in the star of Rahu, a 
Situation of helplessness arises and the power to deliberate on family matters gets inhibited 
because of Rahu’s placement in 2"? house denying the possible action of 3"° house by Moon. 


Examine, if J upiter as another conjunct planet with Mercury and Mars also has to say something. 
J upiter is in the star of Mercury and sub of Mars. J upiter as 6° lord in the star of 12‘ lord 


Mercury and in the sub of Mars (already discussed) completes the ritual of separating the couple 
(6'" and 12" house breaking the walls of attachment in 5°" house). 


Thus, it was evident that Mercury dasha was a very difficult dasha, which had to materialize 
separation without giving any chance to the native to put forth his side. 


In view of this, | was of the opinion that Mercury dasha was very disastrous to cause breakage in 
relationship and no immediate respite was seen to get out of the situation. 


Facts of the case 


The native contacted me later to give me the following facts of the case, which are analysed 
astrologically. 


i 


The separation was inthe form of severe heated arguments, which resulted in separation. 


Dasha lord Mercury has Mars as the sub-sub lord. Mars is 7'" sub-lord and gets closely conjunct 
with the 3" lord Mercury and 9°" lord J upiter indicating mutual dialogues in hot tone. Conjunction 
of Merc-Mars-J upiter in 5'" house, as discussed above, destroys the mutual attachment and cause 
separation. 


The fight between the couples and subsequent separation took place on 6'" Oct, 2006 when the 
native was running the dasha of Merc-Merc-Merc-Merc-Sat. 


The results of Mercury dasha, as analysed, are self-revealing. Saturn is placed in the 6'" house and 
is in sub-sub of 12'" lord- Mercury, sufficient to put the last nail to the separation. 


The parents in law were the chief party to cause the relations to get spoiled. Father-in-law was 
the hero inthis case causing the separation to take place. 


The 3rd cusp indicates Father in law and the 10th cusp indicates Mother in law. 3"° cuspal sub-lord 
is Venus, which is placed in the star of J upiter (6'" lord) joined in the tangle of Mercury-Mars- 
J upiter conjunction indicating discord. 10°" cuspal sub-lord is Saturn, which is in the star and sub 
of Venus. 


Since, Venus (FIL) gives the results of Saturn (MIL) because Venus Is the star lord of Saturn, it 
may be concluded that father-in-law could have enacted the scene and may have been the chief 
executor of effecting separation on the instigation of his wife, just as the star lord effects the 
results of the planet. 


Native has 2 children who have been given to him for their upbringing. His wife has not kept the 
children with her. 


5‘. and 7'" cusp indicate 1°' and 2" child whose sub-lord is Mars. Mercury (dasha lord) is closely 
conjunct with Mars inthe 5‘" house (house of children), thus the dasha did not separate the 
children from him.

The phenomenon of retrogression of planets has always been a tricky and a sticky issue to all those who 
practice astrology sincerely. Predictions have gone haywire due to both consideration and non-consideration of 
retrograde planets. It still remains one of the most discussed yet hardly researched topic in the field of 
modern astrology. This article calls for research frameworks for methodically analyzing the predictive 
outcomes of astrological analysis by taking into consideration the discrepancy between prediction and actual 
outcome in the light of retrograde planets in a large pool of data set. The article will also discuss two horary 
case studies wherein retrograde planets played their necessary roles and created the usual confusion. 

Considerable amount of literature has been spent in the field of Vedic astrology about the role of 
retrograde planets, their effects and their capacity to alter results in nativities. Various rules on the effects 
of retrograde planets have been discussed in ancient texts as well as in modern discourses. But the quality of 
prediction has not improved. |n the last century, with the advent of the Krishnamurti Paddhati technique of 
astrological delineation much clarity has been brought to the fore. Our Gurujl, late Sri K.S. Krishnamurti used 
retrogression of planets with much clarity and simplicity for predictions and timing of outcomes. | t was only 
with Krishnamurti Paddhati that retrograde planets received their due status in prediction and the astrological 
fraternity understood how to use retrogression of planets for prediction. Sri KSK in his six readers formulated 
a number of rules for accurate predictions, the fundamental premise of which is based on retrogression. In 
order to offer prediction for specific queries in the horary chart, our Guruji gave a number of golden rules, 
which when summarized can be stated as follows’: 

1. For every query, find out the most important (main) house, its cuspal sublord and the star lord of this 
cuspal sublord. 

2. Next, find out the houses related to this main house, their cuspal sub lords and the star lords of 
these cuspal sub lord. 

3. The most important house cusp (main) sub lord should not itself be retrograde at the time of 

judgment. 

4. This sub lord should not occupy a star whose lord Is retrograde at the time of judgment. 

5. The main house cuspal sub lord should be related with other house pertaining to the question. 

6. Finally, Rules 3, 4, and 5 should be SIMULTANEOUSLY satisfied to denote a positive answer. If any 

one of the Rules 3, 4 or 5 is not satisfied, it shows a negative result for the querist. Results will not 

fructify. 


lt is therefore, clear that the inventor of this system of astrological prediction placed a lot of 
emphasis on retrogression of planets and its practical utility in prediction. Later authors such as Sri C.R. Bhatt, 
Sri J. Hasbe, Sri M. P. Shanmugam, Sri V. Ramamurthy have equally emphasized in their writing about 
retrograde planet’s capacity to alter prediction. Today in the KP fraternity there appears to be opinion divided 
upon the role of retrograde planets in the light of the above rules. There is one school of thought that 
considers the above rules given by Guruji to be true with respect to both natal and horary horoscopy. The 
second school of thought makes a clear distinction that the above rules of retrogression apply only to horary 


' Refer Readers I to VI authored by Sri K. S. Krishnamurti 


and not to natal horoscopy. Whereas, the third school of thought take a detour and believes that the rules of 
retrogression as propounded by KSK applies to horary only if the main cuspal sublord is in the star of a 
retrograde planet. They do not take exceptions to the cuspal sublords being retrograde. However, no 
systematic research has yet been published to test these Issues. 

Inthe year 1996, late Dr. (Pandit) Kesav Ranjan Kar published an article on retrograde planets in KP & 
Astrology Yearbook. Subsequently another article appeared inthe 1997 issue of the same magazine. Both these 
articles were a landmark paper inthe theory of retrogression of planets for two reasons: firstly, the paper was 
based on his personal research, and secondly, he was able to provide certain pre-tested rules that were 
amenable to further hypotheses testing. Experimentation, testing and inference are the hallmark of a natural 
science and Dr. Kar paved the way for modern practitioners of astrology to take up a new research agenda. 
However, though Dr. Kar’s papers have immense merit in their own respect, today we need research output in 
astrology that would stand the test of rigor and statistical validity. In this respect it is noteworthy that Sri. 
A. R. Raichur and Sri. Kanak Bosmia are doing very commendable, statistically rigorous and valid research 
in KP astrology. |n the April issue of KP E-Zine Sri Bosmia has beautifully summarized the research 
contribution of Dr. Kar with respect to retrogression of planets. 

In this article | suggest a research framework that may assist in operationalizing research in 
retrogression. The purpose of this framework is exploratory in nature and the exact model would be 
determined by the research questions and the hypotheses to be tested in deductive approaches. 


While researching on retrogression of planets in KP, one would need to clearly articulate the 
research question to be addressed. 


This is important both from an ontological as well as methodological point of view. Clear articulation of 
the research question would set the backdrop of the research and the researcher would be better equipped to 
handle data collection, data sorting, data cleaning and subsequent data analysis. To give a few examples, it may 
be worth the time and resource to look into research questions such as: 


1. Does retrogression of main house cuspal sublord deny results? 
2. Does retrogression of auxiliary house cuspal sublord deny results? 
3. Does retrogression of main house cuspal sublord’s starlord deny results? 


Many such valid research questions can be formulated to test various rules and arrive at conclusions. 
Once the research questions have been identified, then a researcher would need to start collecting data 
related to his or her research questions. For example, with respect to the first question above, one may collect 
200 horary and 200 natal charts related to a particular issue, say, child birth wherein the main cuspal sublord is 
retrograde. Once this data has been collected, a researcher would then require categorizing this data in 
appropriate matrices. | provide below an operational design to sort the data for easiness of analysis for natal 
as well as for horary datasets. 


R Yes A

Inthe above 2X2 matrix we find four types of data situations that beckon analysis for testing rules of 
retrogression in KP astrology. The first type is A type wherein the main cuspal sublord is retrograde but 
results were achieved. (An unexpected outcome according to the dictums of classical KP astrology). |nB type 
data situations, the main cuspal sublord was NOT retrograde and results were achieved. (A normal outcome 
according to classical astrology). |n C type of situation the main cuspal sublord is retrograde and no results 
were achieved. (Another normal outcome according to classical KP rules). Finally, in D type of situations, the 
main cuspal sublord was not retrograde BUT no results were achieved. (A situation of anomaly requiring 
inductive research designs). Such situations may arise due to a multitude of factors such as effects of other 
rules, astrologers’ mistakes, etc. Type D data situations are perhaps the most complex wherein the researcher 
needs to be careful about and control for extraneous effects such as astrologers’ mistakes. One practical 
solution to such data situations would be to recast and reanalyze these datasets by two additional astrologers. 
This would help in bringing inter-rater reliability and the much needed data validity in the process of scientific 
inguiry. Once the various types of data situations are analyzed, one may then proceed in systematic data 
analysis with manual tabulation followed by software driven statistical analysis. The results obtained would be 
much more reliable in understanding the efficacy of various rules of retrogression found in classical KP texts. 

The above matrix a simplistic form of data sorting with two parameters. However, in situations 
requiring more than two parameters, suitable modifications in the research design is possible with the guidance 
of an able research supervisor. The design of multi-parametric model should not be viewed as a challenge but 
rather a necessity borne out of practical consideration. Sri Rangarajan Krishnamurty’s research on a couple of 
KP topics is based on such multi-parametric research designs. 

| now provide two case examples to justify the importance of research in retrogression rules in KP 
astrology. The first example is that of a lady whose query was: My monthly menses has stopped. Am | 
pregnant? She gave the KP horary number 248 and | analyzed on the same day—15'" April 2007—at 7:16 pm 
(1ST) in my residence at Hyderabad. The chart is provided below. 

Moon, the reflector of mind and the bearer of the radicality of a horary chart, signifies 5 and 1l. So, 
the question of child birth is reflected in the chart. Moreover, Moon's strong signification of 12'" shows the 
tension and worries at the back of the lady’s mind. 


Since the question is put by a lady, the main cusp that was considered was the 5'" cusp. The 5"" cuspal 
Sublord is Mercury. It is not retrograde. Moreover, Mercury is an A grade significator of 5 and cuspal 
Significator of 5 and 11. At the stellar level, Mercury is also a good significator of 5. Mercury Is in Meena 
rashi—a fruitful sign, and Mercury’s starlord Saturn Is also ina fruitful sign—Cancer. This analysis tempts us 
to pronounce that the lady is pregnant. However, | pronounced that the lady is NOT PREGNANT for a 
simple reason. The reason is also related with retrogression and is part of our 3" question discussed 
above. Even though main cusp sublord, Mercury, is direct, Mercury is inthe star of Saturn which is retrograde 
at the time of judgment. 


This case is a classic example for research questions 1 and 3 discussed above. But one needs to be 
careful in classifying this case. | f we consider only Question 1 then this case falls in Type A, whereas if we view 
it aS an anomaly with respect to question 1, then this case becomes classified as Type D. What we need Is a very 
good number of such case examples where the results can be put to tests for classical KP rules. On 20°" April 
2007 this lady informed me that on this date she had her normal menses, which meant that she was indeed not 
pregnant! 


The second case is about a MBA graduate, Ms. Mittal, who asked me the question when will I get a 
job? She gave me the KP horary number 57 and | analyzed the query on 22™ March 2007 at 1:53 pm (IST) in 
Hyderabad. The lady was working with a multinational but gave up her job due to health reasons and was seeking 
ajob ina better position and pay package. The chart Is provided below. 


Moon, the significator of mind, signified 11 and 2 along with 10 at the stellar level. Thus, the query was 
clearly reflected. The main cusp considered for the analysis was the 6'" cusp. This is because she was curious 
to know about the timing of the job. |t was a case of timing service and therefore, | considered 6" cusp to be 
more appropriate than 10°. Here the 6°" cuspal sublord was Sun signifying only 9 and 3. Sun's sublord Saturn, 
though signified one of the auxiliary houses—namely the 2™ house—it was retrograde. 


NOW THIS WAS A CRITICAL SITUATION. If we consider the first case study to be true and 
reflecting a correct retrogression rule in KP then we should also say that this lady is not destined to get 
a job since the starlord of the main house cuspal sublord is retrograde. This is a typical example of 
dilemma that any astrologer would face. | nthe first case, the retro starlord of the main cuspal sublord did not 
deliver the result. So, by virtue of scientific logic, the same should hold true in this case also and we should 
declare negative result. 


But previous research on retrogression rules by Dr. Kar points out a rule that if Sun is related with 


retrograde main cuspal sublord or its retro starlord or both then there is no effect of retrogression. Note, 
that in this second case, the main cuspal sublord’s starlord--retro Saturn--was the planetary starlord of Sun. 


This direct one-to-one connection of Sun with retro Saturn rendered it powerless to deny results. 

Upon working out the Dasa, Bhukti and Anthara and emphasizing on the Ascendant Starlord of the RP on 
my date and time of judgment, | declared to Ms. Mittal that she would be getting the job and gave her two 
time periods of one week each. The first time period was 22™ to 28" April 2007 and the other was 11'" to 16"" 
J une 2007. On 8'" April 2007 she informed me that she has got an appointment letter from American Express 
Bank for the post of Business Analyst and her joining date was 23"° April 2007. Retrograde planet delivered 
result. 

To conclude therefore, | would like to emphasize on the development of proper research design in 
executing research on various dictums of astrology in general and KP astrology in particular. We need clearly 
focused research questions followed by testable hypotheses for deductive frameworks, rigorous analytic 
techniques with high inter-rater reliability and constant ex-post data testing with the research findings. 
Research in astrology should also conform to norms of scientific testing for greater validity of rules. Only then 
we can predict safely without the attendant danger of making mistakes and drawing the flak of our clients. Sri 
Kanak Bosmia has done a yeoman service to the KP field by publishing KP E-Zine and | would be more than glad 
to offer my guidance for any person who would like to do some serious and systematic research in astrology. 
They may contact me without hesitation.

New FREE FOR ALL software Launching 
J yotishya Deepika version 1.0 


J yotishya Deepika is a state of the art astrology software, catering to KP Astrology as well as the 
branch of classical Vedic Astrology. This attractive Windows® - based software has been produced using the 
State of the art software development technologies from Microsoft and is “future-compliant”. The software 
boasts of the most accurate calculations concerning the cuspal and planetary positions and is based on the 
renowned Swiss Ephemeris. The user interface is extremely simple and at the same time, most attractive, to 
provide a highly intuitive and compelling computing experience. Anybody with exposure to a Windows® - based 
computer system can start working productively with J yotishya Deepika within 30 minutes after installing the 
software. ] yotishya Deepika is a compendium of astrology and the following table summarizes its features: 


a) Cast accurate Natal (Birth) as well as KP Horary (Prashna) Charts 

b) A complete database to store all charts prepared - which can be expanded for “Data Mining” features in 
future releases. 

c) Ayanamsas supported - KP (Original), KP (New) (2003), Lahiri, Fegan Bradley, Usha Shashi, Raman, 
Yukteshwar, Bhasin, Dwjhal-khul and Sayana (Tropical =0 degree ayanamsa). 

d) House cusp systems supported - Placidian, Sripati (Porphyry), Equal House, Equal House with W hole Sign 
(Parashara). 

e) Ability to specify conversion of geographic latitude into geocentric latitude (tan reduction formula 
used). 

f) Other important options that can be user defined:1) Sunrise - whether Disc Center or Disc Edge. 2) 
Rahu and Ketu - Mean or True positions. 3) Orb for conjunction. 4) Duration of an year (365.25 by 
default) - any value the user chooses. 

g) Reports - J yotishya Deepika helps you produce two kinds of reports for Birth as well as Horary Charts - 
concise reports for KP Astrologers and detailed reports (for both KP as well as traditional astrologers). 

h) You choose your own logo to appear on reports and also configure all of your details under “Astrologer 
Details”. 

1) Tools and Utilities: |] yotishya Deepika supports a variety of tools and utilities to support your decision 
making: 1) Planetary Ephemeris Generator (gives Sign Lord, Star Lord, Sub Lord, Sub Sub Lord for each 
planet) 2) Panchanga Generator (gives tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana and lagna ending times also) 3) 
Planetary Retrogression Finder - finds the retrogression of planets for a given year 4) Planet Transit 
Finder - finds transit to any longitude for any planet after a given date and time 5) Ghati-Vighati 
converter 6) Finding the rulers (given a longitude rulers namely - sign lord, star lord, sub lord and sub 
Sub lord) and points ruled by a given set of planets (by specifying the sign lord, star lord, sub lord and 
sub sub lord) 7) Ayanamsa Calculator - find any of the supported ayanamsas for a given date and time 8) 
Lagna Transit Finder - in a given day find lagna transits upto every minute - giving details of sign lord, 
Star lord, sub lord and sub sub lord. 9) Database Manager - maintain the charts in your database. 

j) Extensive KP Astrology support: 1) Complete list of sign lord, star lord, sub lord, sub sub lord for every 
planet and cusp. 2) Placidian House cusps accurate to the second. 3) Ruling planets for the chart as well 
as the casting time of the chart. 4) 4-fold KP Significators - tabulated planet wise and cusp wise. 5) 1to 
249 number support for KP Horary Charts - facility to generate random horary numbers.

1,.THREE KPAYANAMSAS 
1.1. There are three KP Ayanamsas, namely 
|) Original or Old KP Ayanamsa, 
ll) KP Straight Line Ayanamsa , and 
lil) New KP Ayanamsa. 
2.ORIGNAL OR OLD KP AYANAMSA (OKPA) 


2.1. This is Ayanamsa given by Guruji KSK in K.P. Reader |. Based on 291A.D as the year of coincidence 
of both Sayana and Nirayana zodiacs or the year of zero ayanamsa and the annual precession rate of 
Newcomb’s 50.2388475 sec per year, the ayanamsa values for the year 1840 to 2001 were given in deg. 
and min. only. The formula was not given and for years beyond 2001 the Newcomb’s rate Is to be added 
per year to the ayanamsa for 2001. The K.P. Ayanamsa values are usually given in K.P. ephemeris, for 
instance for the year 1900 to 2040 in “Krishnamurti’s Nirayana Ephemeris 1961-1970 by Mahabala”. 


2.2. Formula for the OKPA given by Mr. Neville Lang (developer of Astracadabra) 
OKPA =B +[T* P +(T*T * A)]/ 3600 


where, 

B =Base =22 +1320 / 3600 (22d:22m:00s for 1) an 1900, @00:00 UT) 

T =Y-1900, Y=Calendar year for which ayanamsa Is required 

P =Annual precession rate of Newcomb’s 50.2388475 sec per year 

A =Annual precession rate adjustment of 0.000111sec per year (included for proper "fit" of the values 
given originally in K.P. Reader | ) 


2.3. The Old KP Ayanamsa was presumed to be constant for the full calendar year. However, the 
Krishnamurti Ayanamsa values for the Year 1861 to 2103 in deg., min., sec. and a Table of Ayanamsa for 
Any Day of the Year given in “Astrological Tables for All by Shri Eshwara Manu” published with the 
blessing of Guruji KSK are supposed to support a manual calculation of the Old KP Ayanamsa value 
correct to seconds and for any date in the calendar year. Nowadays it may be a common practice in 
most astrological SWs to use the OKPA value for any date in the calendar year by applying “T“ as 
decimal year inthe form of Year inthe above Mr. Neville Lang’s formula. 


2.4. Late American Astrologer Richard Houck said that the ayanamsha (in his word) values used in his 
book (The Astrology of Death, 1994) --- are generally within about a minute of the popular Krishnamurti 
ayanamsha. (Ayanamsha values for the year 1900 to 2000 in deg., min., sec. are given in pages 40-41 of 
his book eg. 22d:22m:45s for 1900, 23d:04m:17s for 1950, 23d:46m:01s for 2000.) 


2.5. 1n Dr. ] agdish Maheshri’s KP based book, “It’s All in Timing, 1977”, the Old KP Ayanamsa is 
calculated as per the above formula in 2.2 with the same Base “B“ and “T“ but different P =50.2564 


and A = 0.000222, which are similar to the Lahiri Ayanamsa calculation in 3.2. (Formula is given in page 
31 of his book.) 


2.6.1t is worthy to know from Mr. Neville Lang that if a precession rate value Is not equal to Newcomb’s 
50.2388475 sec (eg. 50.2564 in Dr. J agdish Maheshri’s formula), then the annual precession rate 
adjustment value “A“ commonly used is 0.000222. 


2./. The Old KP Ayanamsa is used as the correct ayanamsa in Mr. Umang Taneja’s KP book, “Nadi 
Astrology, Accurate Predictive Methodology, 2002’ and ayanamsa values are given in pages 190-192. 


2.8. The Old KP Ayanamsa used by late Shri Chandrakant R. Bhatt is given for the year 1901 to 2000 in 
his book, “Further Lights on Nakshatra Chintaman, 1980”, page 249. 


2.9. After the adoption of the New KP Ayanamsa Inthe K.P. & Astrology magazine 2003, the Original KP 
Ayanamsa has been known as the Old KP Ayanamsa. 


3. LAHIRI AYANAMSA (LAHIRI ) 


3.1. While the controversy of the correct Ayanamsa was going on, the Lahiri Ayanamsa was adopted in 
the Universal Table of Houses (UTOH), though not so stated. (Thanks to Shri Raichur, co-author of the 
UTOH, for clarification.) 


3.2. Lahiri Ayanamsa Formula 
(as inthe UTOH given by Shri K. Hariharan in “Notable Persons & KP”, pages 75, 138, 153) 


LAHIRI =B +[T* P +(T*T * A)]/ 3600 


where 

B = Base =80890.1535 sec =22d:28m:10s @ lApr 1900 

T =Y-1900, Y=Calendar year for which ayanamsa Is required 

P =50.2564 (for 1900) (Annual precession rate as per modern astronomy) 
A =0.000222 sec per year (Annual precession rate adj ustment ) 


Note: 285 A.D is taken as the year of zero ayanamsa. 


3.3. Referring Shri Lahiri’s statement, Shri Kuppu Ganapathi has explained about 3 sec. difference 
between True and Mean values of the Lahiri Ayanamsa, eg for 1] an 1990 Lahiri Ayanamsa: True value 
(after taking into account of the Nirayana Longitude of Rahu) is 22d:27m:59s and Mean value is 
22d:27m:56s). Such a small difference may not affect any calculation even up to Sub Sub Sub level. 


4. KP STRAIGHT LINE AYANAMSA (KPSTLA) 


4.1.1t is known from Shri Raichur that there was a lot of discussion on the old KP ayanamsa in K.P. & 
Astrology magazine, mostly by Shri M.G.G. Nair and others. But the editor simply barred the discussion, 
and Sri K.M. Subramaniam of “Sub Lord Speaks" just would not change his views on 2 figures as given 
by Guruji KSK, le. year 291 A.D. of zero ayanamsa and Newcomb’s rate of 50.2388475 sec. So a 
Straight line simple formula was assumed using those two figures, though Guruji KSK never said so. 


4.2. KP Straight Line Ayanamsa Formula 
(provided by Dr. Rangarajan Krishnamoorthy, developer of KPAstro 2.7) 


KPSTLA =T*P/ 3600 


where 

T =Y- 291 (Year of zero ayanamsa) 

Y =Calendar year for which ayanamsa Is required 

P =50.2388475 sec per year (Newcomb’s annual precession rate) 


4.3. The KP Straight Line Ayanamsa such calculated up to any date in the calendar year by using “T” in 
the above formula as fractional/ decimal year taking days between given date and 15th April is called KP 
Straight Line (Adjusted) Ayanamsa. 


4.4.1n Shri Raichur’s view, the Newcomb’s rate is to use only for finding the ayanamsa beyond 2000 and 
not fromthe year 291A.D. as some have incorrectly presumed. The assumption of a constant precession 
rate is not valid and a correction Is made once in 100 years. This correction factor is given by Lahiri, by 
Surya Siddhanta, and by the New KPA formula in 2003. This straight line ayanamsa value does not 
match the figures given by Guruj! KSK himself, in his KP Reader | (original edition) for 1840 to 2000, 
year by year. 


4.5. The KP Straight Line Ayanamsa value is different from the Old KP Ayanamsa about 5-6 min.(as 
Shown in 6) despite the application of the original year 291 and Newcomb’s rate. The exclusion of the 
base “B” is the mathematical reason for this difference. Another exclusion of the precession rate 
adjustment factor is supposed to be affected after along time since its effect is accelerating from 1.11 
sec. for 100 years to 4.44 sec. for 200 years, 9.99 sec. for 300 years etc. 


4.6. Surprisingly the KP Straight Line Ayanamsa value is so close to the Lahiri Ayanamsa (as shown in 6) 
that it looks like the Lahiri Ayanamsa in the articles, which used this straight line ayanamsa, in the old 
K.P. & Astrology magazines. Some KP astrologers could make correct predictions by using this straight 
line ayanamsa. |n some astrological books of a new theory, this straight line ayanamsa is used but 
misnamed as the New KP Ayanamsa and misstated its closeness to the Old KP Ayanamsa perhaps due to 
the misunderstanding of the UTOH ayanamsa as the Old KP Ayanamsa but in reality the UTOH 
ayanamsa Is the Lahiri Ayanamsa as mentioned in 3.1. 


4.6. |t is worthy to learn from Shri Raichur that the small difference in ayanamsa used by various KP 
astrologers need not bother a new comer unduly. The important elements in KP are the ‘star lord and 
the sublod’. |n almost all cases, a slight change in the ayanamsa does not change these important 
elements. A new comer should go to the essentials, rather than worry about the technicalities of 
ayanamsa. |n fact, The Times of Astrology magazine publishes articles, which use the Lahiri Ayanamsa, 
with a difference of 6 min. approximately from the KP Ayanamsa, and the KP system of division. | t has 
been found that in almost all cases, except borderline cases, the Star/Sub Lords are the same as the 
ones with the accurate KP ayanamsas. The Sub-Sub lord will change, as it is more sensitive. 


4.7. However, a5 min. difference in ayanamsa value will make a difference in dasa balance at birth from 
13.5 days for Sun dasa to 45 days for Venus dasa through Moon position. Such difference will affect 
the timing of event at Sookshma level as has been found in Kanak Bosmia’s research study mentioned in 
7.2. 


5. NEW KP AYANAMSA (NKPA) 


5.1. New KP Ayanamsa Formula 
(given by Prof. K. Balachandran in KP & Astrology magazine 2003, pages 88-89) 


NKPA =B +[T* P +(T*T * A)]/ 3600 

where 

B =22+1350/3600 =22-22-30 @ 15 Apr 1900 

P =50.2388475 (Newcomb’s annual precession rate) 

A =0.000111 sec per year (Annual precession rate adj ustment ) 


Note: 23 March, 291A.D. is assumed as date of zero ayanamsa 


5.2. 1t is known from Shri Kuppu Ganapathi that a similar formula was also given by Shri M.G. G. Nair 
who had questioned the Newcomb’s rate and desired a correction for this. 


5.2. AS Shri Raichur explains, after alot of discussions, letters etc., the correct KP Ayanamsa had been 
fixed by Prof. Balachandran, and was published in the KP & Astrology magazine 2003, pages 92-93, 
together with Guruji KSK’s second son and magazine editor K. Subramanium’s declaration that the values 
of ayanamsa published supersedes all the previous Tables of ayanamsa published in K. P. Reader | and all 
ephemeris (Krishman & Co.), K.P.T.O.H. and H.T.O.H. etc. 


5.3. There is not any significant difference between the Old and New KPAs. The New KPA gives a 
formula for calculating the ayanamsa correct to seconds and for any date inthe calendar. The formulas 
for New and Old KPAs in 2.2 and 5.1 are basically the same, except the base “B” is taken up to seconds 
inthe New KPA. 


5.5. The difference between NKPA and LAHIRI 


i) The year of zero ayanamsa is 291A.D.for NKPA and 285 A.D. for LAHIRI; 

it) The annual precession rate is Newcomb’s 50.2388475 sec for NKPA and 50.2564 sec for LAHIRI as 
per modern astronomy; 

li!) The annual precession rate adjustment is 0.000111 for NKPA and 0.000222 for LAHIRI; 

iv) The difference in value is about 5-6 min. (as shown In 6) depending on the year under consideration 
due to different annual precession rate and annual precession rate adjustment factor.

7.SOME OBSERVATIONS 


7.1. Shri Raichur says that ultimately, it is not a question which ayanamsa is correct, but ‘using KP which 
ayanamsa gives us the more accurate predictions?’ 


7.2. |t has been found in the KP researcher Kanak Bosmia’s study on around 120 life events of 15 AA 
rated charts that the New KP Ayanamsa Is working better than Lahiri Ayanamsa in the application of KP 
rules, especially at the Sookshma, fourth dasa level. This finding is consistent with the following saying. 


7.3. There is a saying that the KP Ayanamsa is more accurate for Vimshottari dasa and the Lahiri 
Ayanamsa for division charts. However, In a comparative review of 8 ayanamsas (Mod 
Yukt.,.Yukteshwar, Raman, Krishnamurti, Lahiri, Rosicrucian, Fag-Bradley, Deluce), the Krishnamurti 
Ayanamsa, the closest one to Lahri Ayanamsa (except Rosicrucian which is almost the same as Lahir1), is 


the only one ayanamsa which gives all the same J aimini’s Karakas, Navamsha, Saptamsha, Dwadashamsha 
and finer divisions of Chaturvimshamsha (1/24), Shashtyamsha (1/60) like the Lahiri Ayanamsa. (K.N. 
Rao: Timing Events Through Vimshottari Dasha, 1996, Preface to the Second Edition) 

7.4.1 na study of comparing ayanamsa (Lahiri, Raman and Chandrahar!) on the case of Rabindra Tagore, 
a Vedic astrologer concluded that the real ayanamsa should be between the Lahiri and Raman 
Ayanamsas. Infact, the KP Ayanamsa is between the Lahiri and Raman Ayanamsas(as shown in 6). 


8. CONCLUSION 


8.1. Needless to say, nowadays KP followers and KP SWs are using the New KP Ayanamsa adopted in 
2003.1t can be useful for other astrologers too like the Lahiri Ayanamsa. 


8.2. The choice of Ayanamsa (out of around 30 available) is up to the preference of an astrologer 
finding best for him and there is no need to discuss the correctness of ayanamsa which may depend on 
the rules applied by different schools of thought.

W hat is the use of Theory of short prediction (TSP) 


Theory of short prediction (TSP) is very effective when we need the answer into YES or NO. 

Many a time we are asked the question the answer of which can be YES or NO and there is no room for 
WHEN? At such times this TSP works very well. For example, "Will | get job in ABC Company?" “Will | 
get club membership today?” “Will | get number 1 to 5 in my exam?” etc. For queries like this one can 
predict fairly accurately by using TSP. 


Difference between Gulbarga Theory and TSP 


TSP is modification of Gulbarga Theory; but there is vast difference in both. As per Gulbarga theory, if 


the Asc sub lord is the same as Moon star lord, the result is positive. Later it was suggested that if sub 
lord of Asc is star lord of Fortuna the answer is Positive. But, in TSP main difference is there is no room for 
sub in TSP while the Gulbraga theory is based on sub. Also, TSP not only goes up to star lord but adds sub 
sub lord and Asc star and sub sub lord too. Dr. Kar does not suggest about Fortuna but we have to check it 
and do research on the connection of Fortuna in getting answer. 


How to calculate planetary position in TSP 


Planetary position considered here inthis method would be based on! ndian meridian (82 Deg.30Mnt) at 
5.30 AM basis and not otherwise. For example one starts work at Agra or Ahmedabad, Baroda or 
Banglore, Chennai or Chandigarh, at 4.25 p.m. or 5.25 p.m.; 7 a.m. or 8 a.m.; 10 a.m. or 10 p.m.; but he has 
to take time only morning 5.30 a.m. We need only Horary Asc., so no need for other cusp calculation. So,

How to get answer? 


We have to check three conditions as below. There is no special rule to give more importance to any of 
the rules; but we follow with majority answer. |f we found two yes, our answer is Yes; if we found two 
NOs, our answer is NO. Note that there is no roomfor sign and sub in TSP. Calculate Planetary position 
for 5.30 a.m whether you are in Ahmedabad or Andaman, Cochin or Kashmir - because we have fixed Asc 
with us and we don’t need any more calculations for other cusps. Planetary position for 5.30 a.m. is same 
all over in| ndia. Main deciding factor in TSP is Asc sub sub lord. 


1) Note down sub sub lord of Asc sub sub lord. (Horary sub sub lord A is inthe sub sub of planet B, 
in this case B is deciding factor). Now tally Planet B with Moon star lord or sub sub lord. | f 
tallies (in other words, if B is star lord or sub sub lord of the MOON) the answer is YES.If not, 
check with Asc star lord and sub sub lord, if tallies (in other words, if B is star lord or sub sub 
lord of Asc.) the answer is YES. 

2) Note down F-1, star lord if Asc sub sub lord. (Planet A is in the star of B, Please read detailed 
article by the same author in Feb-Mar 2007 KP Ezine issue). Now tally planet B with the Moon 
star lord or sub sub lord. If tallies (in other words, if B is star lord or sub sub lord of the 
MOON) the answer is in YES. 1f not, check with Asc star lord and sub sub lord. |f tallies (in 
other words, if B is star lord or sub sub lord of Asc.) the answer is inYES. 

3) Lastly check with F-3, (Planet A—sub sub lord of Asc—is in the sub sub of planet B. Planet B Is 
in the star of Planet C. In this case, Planet C is the deciding factor). Now tally Planet C with

MOON) the answer is YES.1If not, tally with Asc star lord and sub sub lord. If tallies (in other 
words, if Cis star lord or sub sub lord of Asc.) the answer is YES. 


Role of Node in TSP. 


|f Node becomes a deciding Factor (If in Rule 1, “B”; in rule 2, “B” and, in Rule 3, “C” is Node), then we 
have to check the Planet whose agent Is the Node in below condition: 


A: Star lord of the Node; B: sign lord of the Node; C: Conjoined Planet; D: planet who aspects the node. 


|f any one of “A”, “B”, “C”, “D” becomes the star lord or sub sub lord of the Moon or star lord or sub sub 
lord of Asc., the answer is YES. 


Special Rules 


1) If sub sub lord of Asc is Moon, the result is always positive. 

2) |f Moon is in the star of Sat and the Moon Is aspected by Sat itself, the result becomes 
Negative |.e. NO.1f Sat-Moon are conjoined but connected with the sun by way of conjunction, 
Star or aspect, result comes in a delayed way. 

3) If sub sub lord of Asc is equal to Moon star lord or Asc star lord, the result is always positive 
le. YES.

is the same, so there is no value of this rule and | request the readers not to use this 
rule blindly.

When shall train arrive? A KP appraisal 


Effort by 
Vijay Kumar 
Senior Manager, C-DOT 
Electronic City, Phase-1, Hosur Road 
Bangalore - 560 100 
080-25119580 (Off), 26587463 (Res) 0-9845039153 


v kumar@cdotb.ernet.in 





My family was to reach Bangalore by train on 18-05-2007 and! had to goto the station to pick them up. 
Onthe same day morning, | had the strong urge to find what time the train would reach Bangalore. The 
scheduled arrival of the trainwas 12 50 Hrs IST. 


Horary number 97 flashed in my mind to get the answer. The prashna chart for the horary number 97 is 
produced here. 


This prashna was casted after | reached the office and wanted to observe quickly, as | had to proceed 
for pickup after finishing a lot of office work. 


The chart is being analysed as follows: 


The Query 


My mind was focused to Know the status of train arrival. Look to the position of Moon, which appears tn 
3-7-11'" cusp indicating travel and meeting family on arrival. Thus, the mental focus on the query was 
represented inthe prashna chart. Hence, it was OK to proceed for analyzing the query. 


The co- ordinates for judgment 


|n reader 6,1 remembered having read “Urge comes to one when Moon touches the most sensitive point 
of the zodiac which indicates about the particular matter in question”. 


Taking clue from this statement, it may be observed that when Lagna transits the sensitive point 
indicated by the Moon, the arrival of the train may fructify. Lagna is taken as the event had to fructify 
Shortly. 


This analysis is based onthis principle. 
Analysis of the chart 
e Look for the promise of fructification of event, which would be possible, if the 11'" cusp links to 
the required cusps. Here, 11'" sub-lord Moon is also the sub-lord of 3°° and 7'" cusps. Since, the 
Moon Is placed in its own sub, the results repeat and the meeting with the family was indicated. 
e Whether the train arrival shall be in time or late etc shall be examined by the 11'" cuspal sub-lord. 
Here, Moon is the sub-lord of the 11'" cusp and falls in its own star and hold the sub-lordship of 3°° 


cusp. Thus, it was concluded that the train should be near to its scheduled time or even bef oretime. 


e At the time of prashna, Moon was transiting in Venus (Sign lord), Moon (Star lord), Venus (sub-lord) 
and J upiter (Sub-sub lord). While, there is no planet inthe star of J upiter, Ketu falls inthe star of 


Venus and Mercury falls in the star of Moon. Thus, the position of Moon is jointly governed by 
Venus-Moon-] upiter-Ketu-Mercury. Here, Ketu disposes Sun (Sign lord) and Venus (Star lord) in 
which it transits. 


From the 11'" cusp, the indication of train reaching near to its scheduled time is indicated. Since, 
the scheduled time for the arrival of train was 1250Hrs IST, 1 checked up the Lagna to transit

New Thoughts in Binomial Predictions: An Analysis of 
World Cup 2007 Failed Predictions with Theory of Short 
Predictions (TSP) 


Prof. Andrew Dutta 


Faculty Member, The ICFAI Business School, 
Survey No. 156/157, Dontanapally, Shankerpally 
Mandal, R. R. District, A. P. 501 203, India 
Cell: 0-0-98666 20483 


Email: andrewinfinitum @ yahoo.com 





OM GANESHAYA NAMAHA 


Success is the ability to go from one, failure to another with no loss of enthusiasm. 
- Winston Churchill — British politician (1874 - 1965) 


| ntroduction 

I[n the science of astrology there are often situations when the direction of the outcome is 
more important than the inherent attribute of the outcome itself. Clients and querists may be more 
interested to know in which side the result is going to be tilted rather than the innate happenings in the 
outcome. For example, people might be interested to know whether the person will win or lose, whether 
a person will live or die, whether a person will get the job or not, or whether his country will win inthe 
game or not. These are all situations where the expected results have a binomial outcome. | n other 
words, an astrologer may have to answer questions where the querist is only interested to know whether 
the answer is favorable to him or not; that is, whether the answer is Yes or No. The querist is not 
Interested to know ‘when’, ‘how’ or ‘why’ such outcome will happen simply because he has a clear 
indication of these factors in his mind and therefore, he has no innate urge to Know these from the 
astrologer. For example, a minister contesting an election may simply be interested to know whether he 
IS going to win or his opponent is going to win. His focal interest lies in knowing a Yes or No for himself. 

[t Is primarily for the above situations that late Dr. (Pandit) Kesav Ranjan Kar from Bolani, 
Orrisa invented and provided the astrological community with his Theory of Short Predictions (TSP). 
The first article on TSP was published in the KP Yearbook 2002 and then inthe years 2003 and 2004 a 
few more articles were published by Dr. Kar on the same method. The fundamental philosophical basis 
of TSP is rooted inthe concept of binomial predictions without any focus in root cause analysis. Dr. Kar 
gave TSP to the astrological community to answer questions which have a definite Yes or No type of 
outcomes. His TSP was neither meant to check the honesty of the querist, nor give any reason for the 
outcome or the timing of the event. The epistemological basis of TSP rules out the possibility of 
addressing these issues also which perfectly justifies the applicability of this method. | n other words, 
it would be fallacious on the part of querists or astrologers to try to find out the genuinity of the 
query, or the timing of the event or the reason behind the outcome. Dr. Kar’s method of TSP Is designed 
to answer yes or no type of questions. 

[nthe last few months the editor of this esteemed magazine, Shri Kanak B. Bosmia, has made a 
very commendable and laudable effort in making predictions of World Cup Cricket 2007 cricket 
matches through the application of the TSP method. Shri Bosmia’s effort is commendable and laudable 
because not only he used a technique which is new in approach but he also posted his prediction publicly 
along with his analysis on an internet forum for public appraisal and scrutiny. Shri Bosmia has shown the 
courage that many practioners of astrology may dare to show due to fear of losing face over wrong 
prediction. But our esteemed editor has taken a lot of pains and immense courage to provide predictions 
of all the 51 matches of the World Cup Cricket 2007. 

Shri Bosmia’s predictions are very important to us for three reasons. Firstly, he is the only one 
person in this whole world who has consistently offered unequivocal predictions on world cup cricket 
this year based on the TSP method. Secondly, he has given clear logic behind all his predictions openly 


and publicly thereby giving the scope to the scientific minded people to take up future research in TSP. 
His 51 predictions form a very important repository of TSP based predictions. Lastly, and most 
importantly Shri Bosmia’s all 51 predictions were based on the same set of rules of TSP but results 
varied. This proves that neither Dr. Kar’s rules are wrong nor that Shri Bosmia made any wrong 
application. And this brings us to conclude that if TSP rules, as provided by Dr. Kar is correct and its 
uniform application in 51 cases have also been mantained then there is something that is yet to be 
discovered. 

lt is solely for this last reason that | have done this small, exploratory research on the 12 
failed predictions that were attempted through TSP. The main purpose of this article is to support 
Shri Bosmia in his effort to strengthen the TSP method. The aim of this article is to complement 
the effort of Shri Bosmia in identifying the common pattern or thread present in the 12 failed 
predictions. This article is meant to identify certain issues that may be found common across the 
12 failed predictions of world cup cricket matches. 

This article therefore, may help future researchers in the area of TSP to look in to various 
undiscovered issues which Dr. Kar may have given to us had not his untimely demise in 2004 deprived us 
of a great mind in KP astrology. The findings of this research initiative of mine does not challenge 
any fundamental tenets of TSP as advocated by Dr. Kar and applied by Shri Bosmia, but it 
provides insights in certain issues for further structured research to be taken up in the area of 
TSP. 

My Kudos to Shri Kanak ji for his untiring efforts inthe field of KP astrology in general and TSP 
in particular. This research initiative would not have happened had Kanak ji not made all his 51 
predictions boldly like a true scientist along with his personal encouragement and guidance that | 
received whenever | faced any difficulty with TSP. 


Objective of this Study 

By virtue of positivist scientific reasoning and logic, if a rule, A holds true in 100 situations then 
it must also hold true in the 101° situation assuming that there has been no deviation in its mode of 
application and the rule remains unaltered. If rule A, after holding true in 100 situations fail in the 101* 
Situation, then on the assumptions made above, we need to reexamine rule A once again before we can 
take It as an infallible rule (Bryman, 2001). On similar logic it was observed that all the 51 world cup 
cricket match predictions provide to us by Shri Bosmia, the same rules of TSP were applied diligently in 
all the 51 cases. However, only 12 actual match results were different than that of the prediction made. 
Now if 39 matches yield correct result with the same set of TSP rules applied equally, then logically we 
can conclude that there is some missing link inthe present state of rules. 

The objective of this research is to attempt an exploratory study to find out the 
commonalities, if any, present in the set of 12 predictions of world cup that did not yield 
consistent result. |n other words, the objective of this research is to see what common factors are 
found across these 12 predictions. This study therefore, does not offer any new rule in TSP but paves 
the way for future researchers to take up new research initiatives based on these findings. 


Data Collection 
The data for this study was collected from the email messages that were publicly available to 
me as a member of an internet forum on KP astrology. These email messages were the predictions made 
by Shri Kanak Bosmia for all the 51 cricket matches along with the rules that he consistently followed. 
All the 51 messages were copied and pasted in a word document that served as the initial repository of 
data. Later, 12 messages were identified where the actual match outcome was different from that of 
the predicted one. These were further validated through the official roster of | CC. 


Data Analysis 
Firstly, the data on the 12 matches were rechecked for the horary number and the ascendant 
Cuspal positions that were originally used. Secondly, the planetary positions were rechecked for 5:30 
AM (IST) at the | ndian Meridian (82°E30 ) for the days on which the analysis was originally attempted. 
These two were considered important in order to ensure that there is no noisy data and that there is no 
data in our data set that do not strictly adhere to the Day Rise Planetary Effect (DRPE) principle of Dr. 
Kar. 


Conceptually Ordered Pattern Matching Matrices (COPMM), as suggested by Miles and 
Huberman (1994), were used to tabulate the data for all the 12 matches. All the 12 matches were 
checked with 5 basic rules advocated by Dr. Kar. These are: 


Rule A: YES, if the sub-sub lord (SS) of the Number sub-sub lord (SS) is equal to the 
Ascendant cuspal points |.e. sign or star or sub or sub-sub 


Rule B: YES, if the SS lord of the number SS lord is same as the Moon star. 
Rule C: YES, if the Number SS lord is equal to the Moon star. 


Rule D: YES, if MST Fl (i.e. the star lord of the number SS lord) is same as the Moon 
Star, and 


Rule E: YES, if MST F3 (i.e. No. SS lord (A) in SS of planet B and planet B in star of 
planet C. This C is F3) is equal to the Moon star. 


Apart from the five basic rules above, the COPM™M also contained five other concepts from the 
data set to allow emergence of patterns. These are provided in the COPMM table at the end of this 
article. 

Results 

The pattern that emerged across the 12 predictions was very intriguing. | believe that the 
observations that came out of analyzing these 12 failed predictions need further testing on a wide 
number of charts having TSP based predictions. My findings below are only to initiate others into 
deeper research and constantly check whether better rules can be obtained 


1. Whenever the number SS lord and the SS lord of the No. SS lord is a Node or a retrograde 
planet, the result was opposite to that of predicted result. 


2. Exception to retrogression happened only in 1 out 12 cases where Sun was the number SS 
lord, thereby negating the retrogression effect. 


3. Whenever the star lord of the number SS lord and/or the C of F3 is a node, the result was 
Opposite. 


4. Only DRPE at the I ndian Meridian of 82E30 yielded consistent results. Three out of the 12 
failed predictions could have been correct if the DRPE at the | ndian meridian was used. 

5. Horary number beyond the specified limit of 9, 249, or 2193 directly showed the final 
outcome (in the negative) and no further analysis was required. 


Therefore, the analysis was able to explain all the variation in the 12 cases. 


Implications of the Findings 

The first and foremost implication of the findings is that we need more research with more 
number of failed predictions based on TSP. Even though 12 data sets were good enough to do this 
exploratory study, yet for a statistically valid research we need a large sample size. Secondly, the 
results beckon us to carefully handle Nodes and retrograde planets in TSP prediction. This is important 
because it is a fundamental assumption in KP horary that a retro planet will not deliver results till it 
becomes direct. With the same analogy we can say that since TSP is about very short term prediction, 
we need to be careful about the presence of retro planets at sensitive decision points like SS lord of 
the No. SS lord and the C of F3 during the time when we expect the results to be delivered or 
happening. 

Thirdly, obtainment of horary numbers beyond the specified limits needs to be carefully 
handled. Though Dr. Kar has himself pointed out in his article of 2004 that any number can be taken for 
TSP beyond any limit, we need sufficient research on this before we can accept this practice for the 


simple reason that horary number beyond specified limits goes against the philosophical basis of 
Prahsna charts. 


Scope for Further Research 

Shri Kanak Bosmia ji has created a very good repository of datasets for TSP based on his 51 
predictions of World Cup Cricket 2007. This research would not have been possible had Shri Bosmia not 
placed all his predictions on the internet. What we need today is more number of predictions based on 
TSP, which would be available for systematic research. 

The findings from this study needs to be reexamined in the light of more number of TSP based 
predictions both successful and failed in order to ensure that the astrological community is better 
equipped to help mankind. Even though TSP is based on a few basic rules that was offered to us after 
Some amount of research, we need to take TSP further and try to make it as rigorous as possible. We 
Should not forget that the inventor of KP astrology, Shri K.S. Krishnamurti practiced and researched 
horary with 108 for decades and threw it out after he found that 249 gives better results. | will not 
conclude anything in this article because no research is ever conclusive. We need to keep on perfecting 
our knowledge through trials, errors and constant observation. 


References:

2. Miles, M.B., and Huberman, A.M. (1994). Qualitative Data Analysis: An Expanded Sourcebook. 
Sage Publications, Thousand Oaks, CA.

KP ACTIVITY 


Report on KP Astrologers’ Forum, I ndia 


For the first time I ndia, a Knowledge generation and sharing forum has been created in the field of 
astrology. The forum, based in Hyderabad, is a unique endeavor to integrate and institutionalize 
astrological knowledge, especially in the field of Krishnamurti Paddhati (KP), but is also open to 
traditional techniques in astrology. 

KPAF started with the initiative of two individuals, Sri Rajendra Nimje, | AS, and his friend Dr. V. V. K. 
Mohan. The Forum was inaugurated on 17'" December 2006 at Taj Belson Hotel in Secunderabad and 
currently there are more than 50 regular members who attend, discuss and contribute astrological 
knowledge in the fortnightly meetings held on every second and fourth Sundays. The forum also has 
members from Europe and the US on its yahoo group (kpastrologers@yahoogroups.com) who also 
regularly send in their comments and views apart from members spread all over the country. Recently, 
the Governing Body has been formed for KPAF, which would be responsible for the administration of 
the Forum inamore structured manner. 

The activities of the KPAF include discussion on various rules found in the classical texts of KP and new 
rules based on research. In every fortnightly meeting, pre-decided blind charts, live case studies, 
unique charts are actively discussed and the views and opinions of the members are documented. S enior 
astrologers from the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad are invited regularly for guest 
lectures to add more value to these meetings. 

On, 22" March 2007, the website of Astrouser (www.astrouser.com) and Astro 3 astrology software 
was launched by the former head of the department of astrology of Telegu University, Sri C. 
Subramanyam ji. The inaugural ceremony was attended by more than 100 guests along with regular 
members. Demonstration of the software was also provided by the developer, Sri Rajendra Nimje and 
was well taken by one and all. Demo CDs were also distributed to members. 

The KPAF has shown the astrological fraternity the need for unified effort in knowledge generation, 
dissemination and documentation. With doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants, bankers, 
professors and businessmen as its regular members, the forum clearly shows how elated minds have 
united to bring back to astrology its lost glory. With the publication of the forums annual journal due at 
the end of this year, the astrological fraternity will immensely benefit from a rich basket of applied 
knowledge. 


Launch of Astrouser and Astro 3 





Mohan ji, Shastry ji and Ninje ji 


Report on Ludhiana KP Activity report 


Two days workshop on Kp astrology was organized recently by kp chapter of ludhiana , at astro-research 
centre , Agar nagar Ludhiana with a objective to focus on accurate predictions basis on both horary and 
natal charts. 30 charts were discussed in a compact and marathon manner, it took 10 hrs each day, the 
presence of participants for the whole discussion is evidence of their immense interest and success of 
the workshop.. Sh. Suresh Shahasne from Mumbai gave two days lecture and describe every aspect of 
predictive astrology in detail. 27 participants were benefited with the workshop from all over Punjab. 
Rupinder kaur , acomputer professional, seema j1, a business lady, mr sharma , an engineer, miss 
chanchal, English teacher, devinder singh, principal from moga, mr bains, lecturer in engineering college, 
Sunita, English lecturer, and others attended full workshop. 

Mrs M.Chatwal, dy manager in FCI , coordinated the workshop very efficiently. Certificated were 
distributed after workshop. 


Next workshop will be planned in October/November.

1, GENERAL RULES 


1.1. Referring KP Readers, Shri Bhatt’s books, Astrosecrets and KP & Astrolgy Year Books and some 
other KP literature, the KP general rules are summarized in the attached table of the KP House 
Grouping for Marriage and Childbirth. Some information on related issues has been provided below. 


2. MARRIAGE RULE 


2.1. |1t is learned form Shri Kuppu Ganapathi that some KP Astrologers are of the view of that 
signification of houses 5 and 8 by the 7th Cusp Sub Lord can also give marriage since 5th is llth to the 
7th and 8th is 2nd to 7th. But GURUJ | LATE SRI K.S.KJ1., INVERNTER OF THIS KP SYSTEM, 
mostly ruled that unless the 7th Cusp Sub Lord signifies either 2, 7 or 11, we can straightaway decide 
that for such a person there will be no marriage at all in his life time. 


2.2. Regarding the 2,7,11 KP marriage houses, 5, 7, 11 houses are taken in a new theory and 2, 7, 11,5, 8 
houses in a new method but only 2,7,11 houses by Shri Bhatt except 5th in some love marriage cases 
only. 


2.3.1 n fixing the DBA, in addition to 2, 7, 11 houses, 3 (negotiation) and 5 (love affair) houses are used 
to be taken by some as supporting houses. Moreover, other houses might be involved depending on 
circumstances such as 3, 9 or 12 houses(a bride leaving her parents’ residence to join the bridegroom's 
family ina far place) and 4, 8 houses (father’s expenditure for her wedding). 


2.4. The general rules are applicable to any chart without discrimination but they are not supposed to 
fit to each and every chart. Here is an exceptional chart of a male of three marriages which can not be

4. KP RULES FOR SECOND MARRIAGE 


4.1.KSK RULE ONE 
(KP Reader VI, page 165 covering the rules in KP Reader | V, page 84, 181 & 182) 


4.1.1. Second marriage Is indicated if the following two conditions are simultaneously satisfied: 


1) The sublord of the 7th cusp is deposited in a dual sign or in the constellation of a planet in or owning 
a dual sign or if the sublord of the 7th cusp is Mercury; and 


2) The sublord of the 7th cusp is also a significator of either of the houses 2 or 11. 
|f any of the above two conditions is not satisfied, then second marriage is denied. 


4.1.2. The KP dual signs are Gemini, Sagittarius and Pisces only, excluding Virgo. (KP Reader ||, page 75) 
As a dual planet in this case of multimarrige only, |] upiter, lord of two dual houses, works well for the 
rule along with Mercury in Kanak’s study on Multimarriage.

(KP Reader | V, page 146) 


4.2.1.1f the sublord of the second cusp is connected with 7th house, second marriage (is promised); (if 
connected with 11th house, one will keep a keep, as 7th house signif icator shows legal bondage whereas 
the 11th indicates attachment and friendship.) 


4.2.2. The 2nd cusp sublord’s connection with 7th is crucial for a legal marriage, otherwise it will be 
keeping a keep or companion or living together only. 


4.2.3. Udaychandra Vaidya: As for first marriage 7th cusp is judged; 2nd cusp to be judged for 2nd 
marriage; if the sublord of 2nd cusp is connected with 7th house, 2nd marriage is promised. (KP & 
Astrology Year Book 2002, page 60) 


4.2.4. The rationale of taking the 2nd house for the second wife is that the 2nd being 8th from 7th 
signifies death of first spouse or 7th house matters. Advocates are Kalidasa, KSK, O.S. Agarwal, Sanjay 
Ruth etc.

9th cusp is a significator of either of the houses 2 or 9 or 11.

7. KPDP MATCHING METHOD BY SHRI KUPPU GANAPATHI 


(KP & Astrology Year Book 1997, page 32-44; also in KP E-Zine March 2007; incorporated in Shri

allotted to mother is very clear. Therefore the 10th house which Is 7th to 4th to be denoted to father, 
will be more appropriate. (Shri Shanmugam: Astrosecrets)

house for father

11.6. CKV METHOD 
(oy Shri C. Kadirvelu; provided by Dr. Rangarrajan Krishnamoorthy) 


http://www.kpastrosystem.com/ docs/ ckv-rule.pdf 


11.6.1. The procedure is: 


1) Take 5th cusp sub lord (CSL). Note whether it is deposited in Male or Female sign. Denote this 
gender by ‘G’, that is, G is either Male or Female. 


2) Count the number of times Rahu or Ketu or Saturn appears as the 5th signlord, star lord or 
Subsublord. Let this count be K. (Note: Sublord is excluded.) 

3) Count the number of times Rahu or Ketu or Saturn appears as the signlord or starlord of the 5th 
CSL. Let this count be L. 

4) Count the number of times Rahu or Ketu or Saturn that appear in the sign where 5th CSL is 
deposited (1.e., conjoined with 5th CSL). Let this count be L. 

5) Add K, Land M. Let the result be N. 

6) 1f N is even number, then G is the guessed gender of the native. | f N is an odd number, the opposite 
of Gis guessed gender of the native. 


11.6.2.1n Diana’s chart, 


1) The 5th CSL Saturn is in Capricorn, Female sign. F =FEMALE 

2) None is applicable. Hence K=0 

3) 5th Sgl is Saturn. Hence L=1. 

4) 5th CSL Saturn is not conjoined with Ra/ Ke/Sa. Hence M=0 

5) N=04140 =1 

6) Since N is odd, the guessed gender is the opposite of G, which is FEMALE, |.e. MALE CHILD.
