A Note on Mean Nodes vs True Nodes 


by 
Tin Win 


tw853@yahoo.com 





Background of Mean Nodes and True Nodes 


1. The Nodes (Rahu and Ketu) are not planets. They are mathematical points 

in Space indicating the intersection of the orbit of the Earth around the Sun 

and the orbit of the Moon which revolves around the Earth. The planes of 

these two orbits intersect each other at 5° 8' 40". The line of intersection is the Nodal axis 
formed by the Nodes. (Alexander Ruperti: Cycles of Becoming, The Planetary Pattern of Growth.) 


2. Inreality, the Nodes “wobble” a bit. They do not move at an entirely predictable speed and vary 
from day to day. They frequently turn, station, travel direct, station and return to a retrograde 
motion. Although the Nodes move around the Zodiac in a retrograde direction, the True Nodes may 
occasionally be direct and are stationary for several days at a time, as if they are wobbling. That's 
because the True Nodes take the gyroscopic relationship of the Sun/Moon into account. The Mean 
Node is always retrograde as said in the scriptures. 


3. Prior to the mid-1970s astrologers only had access to the ‘Mean Nodes" which is the average 
position of their wobbling or motions. The calculation of the Mean Nodes is easy by taking the av- 
erage of motions and the True ones is complicated. However, with the advent of computers and the 
accuracy of ephemerides and diurnal tables increasing by leaps and bounds, astronomers began to 
plot its course of wobbling or motions and call this position the True Node. The American 
Ephemeris programmed by Neil Michelsen and published by Astro Computing Services (ACS) has 
listed both True and Mean Nodes ever since then. Most software programs now have the option 
of Mean or True Nodes whichever one is preferred. 


Are True Nodes Really True? 


4. The main reason of using the True Nodes is that they are the actual measurement of the exact 
positions of Nodes. However, 


1) This is somewhat illusory, since the “True” Nodes are true “only twice" a month when the Moon 
crosses the ecliptic. Other positions provided for the times in between those two points are just 
a hypothesis. 


2) They are based on the idea that celestial orbits can be approximated by elliptical elements. 
This works well with the planets, but not with the Moon, because its orbit is strongly perturbed 
by the Sun. 


3) That is why Robert Hand point out in “Horoscope Symbols” that the wobbling Nodes are no more 
"True" than the Mean Nodes, as they are in their own way just as abstract a concept. They should 
not be used until research has indicated which, if either, of the two sets of the Nodes is more 
valid. 


4) The True Nodes can differ from the Mean Nodes by up to 1 4 degrees and the Moon crosses 
the ecliptic at the True Node, at which time the difference from the Mean Node can be plus/minus 
O to 1 ¢ degrees. There are thus three Nodes for which convincing arguments can be made: (1) 
Mean Nodes (2) instantaneous True Nodes (3) actual True Node nearest a given time. The last 
two can differ by over one degree. (Geoffrey Dean: Recent Advances in Natal Astrology) 


Preference for Mean Nodes 


5. Some views in favor of Mean Nodes are as given under:

lord retro-Jupiter is placed in 10™ house. Thus, Saturn strongly operates 5™ house and 10™

Rahu gets placed in 11 house. The strong stellar disposition of 9™ house by Mars does not 
portend much in store.

getting the job. Let us see further.

Child Gender 


Prediction Analysis 
By 





TIN WIN Dr. K. RANGARAJAN, Ph.D 


1. The total charts of 32 with the number of children considered 150 are analyzed for the 
following four theories of child gender prediction: 


1) As per Theory by V.S.N. Murthy, KP EZine July 2008, A = Cuspal sub-sublord, B = sub- 
sublord of A, C = Sub-lord of B, D = Starlord of C; If D is a Male star, a Male child is 
predicted; if a Female star, a Female child is predicted. 


2) A-simplified Theory of V.S.N. Murthy"s Theory is A = Cuspal sub-sublord, B = Starlord 
of A; If Bis a Male star, a Male child is predicted; if a Female star, a Female child is 
predicted. 


3) According to 4 Step Theory, A = Cuspal sublord, B = Sublord of A, C = Starlord of B; If 
C is in the odd sign, a Male child is predicted; if in even sign a Female child is predicted. 


4) InHora Theory, A = Cuspal sublord, if A is a planet without any planet in its star A itself 
or if A is a planet with any planet in its star, B = Starlord of A is in the Male Hora, a 
Male child is predicted; if ina Female Hora, a Female child is predicted. 


2. AS a common practice, for a female chart 5th cusp for Ist issue, 7th cusp for 2nd issue, 9th 
cusp for 3rd issue, 11th cusp for 4th issue and so on, and for a male chart 11th cusp for the Ist 
issue, Ist cusp for 2nd issue, 3rd cusp for 3rd issue, Dth cusp for 4th issue and so on are 
analyzed. 


3. For the first three theories the analysis is done by the computer program and the fourth 
theory is analyzed manually on the KP charts by KPAstro 3.0 using the New KP Ayanamsa 
adopted in the K.P. & Astrology Year Book 2003. 


4. The correctly predicted numbers out of 200 children and percentages are as given under: 


1) Theory by V.S.N. Murthy -- 86 children (57.3 %) 

2) Simplified V.S.N. Murthy's Theory -- 72 children (48 %) 
3) 4 Step Theory-- 74 children (48.3 %) 

4) Hora Theory-- 70 children (46.7 %)

5 = actual gender of children, 6 = Theory by Murthy's Theory 
7 = Simplified Murthy's Theory, 8 = 4 Step Theory, 

9 = Hora Theory)

Reinstatement of Judges in Pakistan 
by

Will judges in Pakistan be reinstated ? 
This question was asked by a queerest while my live programme on KP was telecasted in Manchester 
tv. The answer was negative. I am discussing the case for academic purpose. 


Horary number- 35 

Date- 29-04-2008 

Time - 20-31 

Place- Manchester - (53-30 N, 02-15W) UK 


Rule 


Note the sub lord of 10th cusp, if this sub lord is deposited in the constellation of the planet 
which is significator of 2 or 6 or 10, he must be reinstated. But if the sub lord of 10th cusp is de- 
posited in the constellation, lord of which is signifying 1 or 5 or 9 or 12 and at the same time not 
signifying 2 or 6 or 10 then he will not be reinstated. (KP Reader VI, page 299) 


Application of the Rule 


Note the 10th cusp sub lord. It is Rahu. 

Now note its constellation lord. It is deposited in the star of Mars. 
Now look whether Mars is signifying houses 2 or 6 or 10 ? 

Mars is in 3 and it is lord of 7. 

Now look what is stellar signification of Mars ? 

Mars is in star of Jupiter. Jupiter is in 9 as lord of 8-9-12. 

Total signification of Mars is 3-7-8-9-12. 

Mars is nowhere connected with 2 or 6 or 10. 

Result will be negative. 


Result 


Judges were not reinstated in Pakistan .

Viswa Guru Bhagawan Sri Veda Vyasa 


Kabir said: "If all the land were turned to paper and all the seas turned 
to ink, and all the forests into pens to write with, they would still not 
suffice to describe the greatness of the guru." 


GURU PURNIMA 


Guru Purnima is traditionally held to be Bhagawan Vyasa's birthday. Accord- 
ing to the Indian calendar it falls on the 15th of the month of Ashada. Bha- 
gawan Vyasa is called Veda Vyasa - or the Compiler of the Vedas. Bhagawan 
Vyasa saw that, in the coming yugas, men would be of grosser mind and would 
lack the ability to learn and retain all of the Vedas. So he compiled the Vedas 
into four parts - the Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva Veda. 


Furthermore he wrote the Puranas so that the common people could also 
benefit from the knowledge of the Vedas - he conveyed the same spiritual 
principles through the medium of stories and parables. He is also the author 
of the Brahma Sutras - the quintessence of Vedanta. So it is but fitting that 
his birthday is celebrated as Guru Purnima. 


This day also heralds the coming of the life-giving rains, the monsoon season 
in India. During this season, sannyasis traditionally stay at one place and en- 
gage in scriptural studies and contemplation. This period is called the 
Chaturmasya or literally the four months. Guru Purnima is the day from 
which this period commences. 


Guru Parampara 


A lineage of Gurus and shishyas who themselves became Gurus, and that goes 
back to time immemorial is known as the Guru Parampara. If we trace this 
lineage to its source we find that Iswara Himself must have been the first 
Guru. 





Sri Dakshinamurti 


Sri Dattatreya 
Sadasiva samarambham sankaracharya madhyamam | 
Asmat acharya paryantam vande guru paramparam || 








In ancient India the Gurukula system of education prevailed. On reaching 
the age of eight, children were sent to live in the ashrams of the Acharyas 
in order to learn all the scriptures, arts and sciences. There were two types 
of Acharyas. Vedavid - those who knew the Vedas; and Brahmavid - those 
who knew Brahman. It is this latter type of Guru whom we refer to as Sat- 
guru. 


Then there are the Avatara Gurus who take birth at critical junctures in 
history in order to redeem dharma (righteousness), and effect an all-round 
spiritual renaissance. Like the sun in the sky, they illumine the whole world 
with their blazing light of Divinity. On the threshold of a new millennium, 
which is marked by rampant materialism, nihilism, and the dearth of love 
among mankind. This embodiment of Divine Love and Grace, by giving initia- 
tion to millions, has thrown open the gates of spirituality for all to enter. 


On the occasion of this Guru Purnima, 
let us offer our salutations to 
Our Beloved Guru ji Shri Krishnamurti ji 





Jyotisha Maha Guru 
Sri K S Krishnamurti 


Guru Purnima is a day for celebration and worship - a day on which the 
disciples remember and express their gratitude to the lineage of Gurus.

Basic Significators 


1. A planet signifies the matter through the following three levels according 
to the occupation and lordship of the houses: 


1) The planet signifying the source of the matter; 

2) The star lord of the planet revealing the nature of the results of the 
matter; 

3) The sub lord of the planet showing as the deciding factor whether the 
matter is favorable or not. 


2. A star lord is stronger than a planet and a sub lord is more powerful than 
a star lord. KP is the sub lord theory, nothing else. The discovery of the in- 
fluence of the sub lord has added a new dimension to the stellar astrology. 
If the indication at the star level is general, the sub makes it specific. If a 
planet is in the star of the occupant of the 2nd house of finance, but in the 
sub of occupant of the 12th house of loss, the result will be financial loss. 
If the sub lord is a strong significator of 11th house of gain, it is the indi- 
cation of financial gain. If the sub lord is a strong significator of 6th house 
of loan, there will be financial gain through borrowing. 


3. The sub lord is useful as the deciding factor in the following cases: 


1) Whether a planet is auspicious or inauspicious for the house signified by 
that planet according to the sub lord of that planet; 


2) Whether the matter denoted by the house in question is promised or not 
according to the cuspal sub lord of that house; 


3) Whether the DBA lords are favorable or unfavorable for the event under 
study as per their sub lords; 


4) Which sub dasa would give the marriage and which sub dasa would cause 
the divorce during the same dasa by only gleaning from the sub only in KP: 


5) Whether a planet is the strong significator of the houses for which that 
planet is the cuspal sublord depending on whether there is any planet in the 


| star of that planet; 


6) What planets should be selected as the fruitful significators when the 
planets are the significators of many or almost all houses. 


4. The division of star, sub and sub-sub etc as dasa, bhukti, antara and sook- 
shma was known before to find out the timing of an event only. Credit goes 
to Guruji KSK for using these divisions up to the star and sub in the Hindu 
astrology for the first time to examine whether the cusps and planets are 
really fruitful or not. 


5. Guruji KSK has provided his rasi chart together with the navamsa chart 
side by side in the KP Reader III and the unprecedented 3-page detailed 
table of navamsa calculation in the KP Reader I without applying the navamsa 
anywhere. It is perhaps his expression of gratitude to the navamsa for giving 
the idea of nakshatra navamsa or one-ninth division of the nakshatra in the 
manner of Vimshotari Dasa system. 


6. The star lord effect of the dasa lord planets, i.e. analysis of the planet 
together with its star lord, has been taken into consideration since about 
2000 years ago in Satyacharya's Dhruvanadi and nowadays in B.V. Raman's My 
Experiences in Astrology, How to Judge a Horoscope and Notable Horo- 
scopes. Without applying the influence of the sub lord in prediction and the 
Placidus house system in casting a horoscope, it is not KP. Also it is no more 
KP, if the sub is not considered as the deciding factor. 


7. In order to get the better prediction results, all the houses signified at 
all three levels of planet, star and sub are to be jointly considered (like C. 
R. Bhatt, K.M. Subramanium of Sub Lord Speaks, Kanak Bosmia, Umang 
Taneja), for instance: 


1) The houses signified at the first two levels of star and planet are going 
to give the desired results, if they are supported by the sub signification. 
In the context of culmination of the particular event, the planet can be said

Order of Significators 


8. The order of significators from grade A to E preference is as follows: 


A) — Planets posited in the star of the occupant of the concerned house; 
B) Occupant of the concerned house; 

C) Planets posited in the star of the lord of the concerned house; 

D) Lord of the concerned house; 

E) Planets which are in conjunction with or aspected by the significators 


(referring the Original Krishnamurti Padhdhati Vol. 2 <1966> pp 114, 118, 301, 
303, 308; KP Reader IIT pp 342; IV pp 118, 128, 201; V pp 149, 201; VI pp 
157, 197, 247). 


9. Based on the logic of a star lord being stronger than a planet and the oc- 
cupant in a house being stronger than the owner of the house: 


A) A planet in the star of the occupant of a house is stronger than the oc- 
cupant and the planet is the strongest grade A significator of the house oc- 
cupied by its star lord: 


B) If there is no planet in the star of the occupant, then the occupant, grade 
B significator, becomes the strong grade A significator; 


C) The planet in the star of the owner of a house, grade C significator, is 
stronger than the owner, grade D significator, and if the house is vacant, i.e. 
no grade A and B significators, then the planet of grade C significator be- 
comes the strong grade A significator; 


D) If the house is vacant, i.e. no grade A and B significators, and if there is 


| no planet in the star of the owner of the house, i.e. no grade C significator, 


then the owner of the house of grade D significator becomes the strong 
grade A significator of that house. 


E) As the grade A significators are strongest, the weakest grade E signifi- 
cators are generally applied as the last resort. In this regard, Guruji KSK has 
encouraged to apply the Western aspects but not practically applied or ex- 
plained how to deal with the nature of Western aspects like good for trine, 
bad for square, other than to find out the exact distance. (KP Reader I) 
M.P. Snhanmugam's view in Astrosecrets & KP Part 1 that when the outer plan- 
ets (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn) aspect the inner planets (Moon, Mercury, Venus), 
the inner planets are subjected to the significations of the outer planets- 
has been found working in some DBA analysis by Kanak Bosmia. In the exam- 
ple chart, Jupiter aspects Moon and Moon has to give the results of Jupiter 
as per KP signification. As another example; Moon has to give the results of 
Mars in the case of Mars is in conj. with Moon.

Rahu / Ketu Significators 


16. Generally Rahu/Ketu indicates (in KP Readers and Bhatt's Nakshatra 
Chintamani): 


1) Firstly, the results of planet with which it is conjoined; 

2) If no planet is in conjunction, the results of planets aspecting it; 

3) If neither is conjoined nor aspected, the results of the star in which 
it is deposited; 

4) Lastly, the result of the lord of the sign in which it is deposited. 


17. In the review of the practical examples of Rahu/Ketu signification in the 
KP Readers, the findings are as follows: (Details in Rhu/Ketu Rules in KP, KP 
E-Zine, May 2007) 


1) The Hindu aspects of house to house and conjunction in the same rasi 
are used; 

2) Aspect of Rahu/Ketu is not applied at all; 

3) The importance of strong significators is considered whenever appropri 
ate by taking into account of the occupation of star lord, Rahu/Ketu in 
own star, Rahu/Ket having no planet in its star and the empty houses. 

4) Although it is quoted "only when it is neither conjoined with, nor aspected 
by any planet, it represents the sign lord" , whether Rahu/Ketu being in 
position of planet or star lord or sub lord, the results of the followings 

are taken into consideration depending on relevance to the matter under 
consideration regardless of their sequence of preference: 


(a) House occupied by Rahu/Ketu, 

(b) Planet in conjunction with Rahu/Ketu, 

(c) Planet in aspect to Rahu/Ketu, and 

(d) Star lord of Rahu/Ketu, 

(e) Sign lord of rasi in which Rahu/Ketu is located.

A Planet Close to the Next House Cusp 


21. An experience of the orb theory (by K.S. Krishnamurti, K.M. Subrama- 
nium, T. Rajendra Kumar, C.V. Tyagaraja Iyer, K. Subramaniam, Carl Woe- 
bcke, Michael McClain, Chandrakant R. Bhatt, Anant Raichur, Sunil 
Gondhalekar, Robert Hand in A Note on the Influence of a Planet near the 
House Cusp, Astrovision, June 2008 ) is that a planet deposited close to the 
next house cusp within 3° 20° orb can give the results of the next house, and 
the planet is considered as if it is in the next house. The tighter an orb is 
within 1°- 2 and no other planet is in the next house, the stronger the signi- 
fication of the next house will be. This is not an additional significator but 
a shift in the signification of a house from the previous house to the next 
one. 


22. If a planet is supposed to have influence on both the previous house, in 
which the planet is physically posited, and the next house, to whose cusp the 
planet is close, the results of the next house may not be effective as the 
previous house is detrimental or Vyaya or negative to the matters of next 
house. (KP Reader III, IV; Bhatt's Nakshatra Chintamani) 


23. In the attached example chart, Mars at 10° Ta 20° 25" is close to the 
Ist cusp at 11° Ta 43° 32" within the commonly used orb of 3° 20°. So, as 
per the orb theory, it is to consider Mars as if it is in the 1st house, although 
it is physically located in 12th house. Since it is very close to the Ist house 
cusp within only 1° 23° orb and there is no planet in the 1st house, Mars will 
give the results of the 1st house other than the matters of 12th house. If 
Mars is supposed to give the results of both 12th and 1st houses, the results 
of 1st house may not be effective as the 12th house is 12th or detrimental 
or negative to the 1st house.

Short History of Zimbabwe : 


On 18 April 1980, the country attained recognition as an independent country 
and along with it a new name, ZIMBABWE, a new Flag, anda Government led 
by Robert Mugabe of ZANU. Canaan Banana served as the first President 
with Mugabe as Prime Minister. In 1987, the Government amended the Con- 
stitution to provide for an Executive President and abolished the Office of 
Prime Minister. The constitutional changes went into effect on 1 January 
1988, establishing Robert Mugabe as President. 


Under the leadership of Mugabe, land issues, which the liberation movement 
promised to solve, re-emerged as the vital issue in the 1990s. Beginning in 
2000, Mugabe began an effort to redistribute land from white holders (pre- 
dominantly large farms) to 250,000 Africans. 


Zimbabwe is currently experiencing a hard currency shortage, which has led 
to hyperinflation and chronic shortages in imported fuel and consumer goods. 
Mugabe's critics blame his programme of land reforms. However, Mugabe 
claims that massive financial isolation through American, British and EU leg- 
islation such as the Zimbabwe Democracy and Economic Recovery Act 
(ZDERA) of 2001 is the actual cause of hyperinflation. Under ZDERA, the 
United States is prohibited from supporting any efforts by the Interna- 
tional Monetary Fund and other financial institutions to extend loans, credit 
or debt cancellation to the government of Zimbabwe. As Zimbabwe needs to 
import all its energy, and oil is paid for in US dollars, this made the country 
vulnerable to financial sanctions like ZDERA. 


Zimbabwe's current economic and food crisis, described by some observers 
as the country's worst humanitarian crisis since independence, has been at- 
tributed, in varying degrees, to government economic mismanagement, gov- 
ernment prohibitions on relief efforts from foreign NGOs (non- 
governmental organizations), a drought affecting the entire region, and the 
HIV/AIDS epidemic.

This article is in continuation to my earlier article regarding the job 
prospects of the ward of my office colleague. In the first week of this 
month, my colleague approached me and informed me about his child who had 
cleared all level of interviews for another job opportunity and was to be in- 
terviewed at the final level and was expecting to join the job thereafter. He 
wanted to know, if things would go well. 


I casted the time chart as he approached me. Since, the query was meant for 
his child, I did rotate the chart to the 5th house. 


The time chart was casted at July 07, 2008 at 17-51-06 Hrs IST at 12N51, 
77E40. The rotated chart is presented herewith. 


Coordinates of judgment: 


- Ina horary chart, lagna may be examined to indicate the resources avail- 
able to the individual with respect to the query. In the present case, it could 
be with respect to the professional prospects. 


- The prospects relating to the profession in the natal chart are seen from 
the 10th cusp, as this is where the karma yoga flows down in the native's 
life. 


- Generally, the 6th cusp/house indicates the work/service or the job in par- 
ticular. With the advent of various dashas, the suitability of the individual 
to the job definition may be delineated. 


- The 5th house has a peculiar functionality with respect to the karma yoga 
seen from the 10th cusp. It is to be noted that the 5th house is 8th from 
10th and thus represents the obstructions, which come on the way of pro- 
fessional fructification. 5th house also supports power, position and recog- 
nition in the work scenario. 


The analysis of the chart: 
A brief snapshot of analysis is presented herewith. 
1. Examine Lagna and Moon 


Sun gets the role as the sub-lord of lagna. Sun is powerful as there is no 


| planet in its star, thus its placement in the chart may be dominating. It is ob- 


served that Sun is placed in 3rd house, which shows that the native was yet 
pursuing the formalities to be completed for gaining the job. This was more 
amply clear when the star lord of Sun was examined. Sun was in the star of 
retro-Jupiter which was placed in 9th house as 9th lord. Thus, it was suf fi- 
cient to infer that there were some formalities pending from the employer's 
side and it was rightfully acknowledged by my colleague. 


Look at the Moon which appears in 6th cusp showing mental concentration on 
the job. Moon being strong is placed in 5th house which shows present un- 
employment. 


Hence, on the face value, the time horary chart looked genuine and it was 
safe to proceed further. 


2. Examine 3-9th cusps 


As the matter was yet in negotiation stage, it was pertinent to look at the 
3-9th cusps closely. 


Incidentally, retro Jupiter lords both 3-9th cusps as the sub-lord. Jupiter 
is placed in the star of Venus as 7th lord placed in 3rd house, showing the 
native's pursuance (3rd house) being the primary driver. Since, Jupiter falls 
in the sub of Saturn which is the 10-11th lord, the efforts of the native was 
indicated to bring the fruition. Due to the involvement of Saturn, there had 
be delays and the matter was destined to be driven in piecemeal. 


Looking to the efforts connected to bring the positive results, it was en- 
couraging to proceed further. 


3. Examine 10th house for professional indications. 


10th cuspal sub-lord is Venus. Venus effectively lords the 7th house, thus 
the job was on the terms of the employer (7th house). Venus falls in the

cases were noticed who are subject to wrong treatment. In this Article two 
natal charts were discussed where the natives were admitted in the hospital 
for treatment were wrongly treated.

1. Referring the statement in Phala Deepika (page 196) for mahadasa calcu- 
lation to take the Solar year, which is the time taken by the Sun to complete 
one round of the Zodiac from any reference position, Guruji KSK has guided 
to adopt the Solar year of 365.25 days alone for calculating the Vimshottari 
Dasa system, and to take 360 days a year for easy calculation of sub sub 
(DBAS) dasa periods. (KP Reader I pp 96-97) 


2. This length of the Solar year is in line with the following references: 


1) According to the present universally used Gregorian calendar, the average 
year is 365.2425 days, which is applied in the SWs like KPAstro 3.0, JHora. 


2) The moderns take the mean length of the sidereal Solar year to be of 
365.2564 days (365d-6h-9m-9.50 sec). 


3) In Surya Siddhanta, the length of the sideral Solar year is 365.2587 days 
(365. gh 15.31.30), which is longer than the above mean length (365.2564) 
by about 3m19sec only. 


4) In Siddhanta Siromani, a Solar year consists of 365.2584 days (365. gh 
15.30.22), which is longer than the above mean length (365.2564) by about 
2m53sec only. 


3. Some remarks on the 360 day year are as given under. 


1) The 360 day year doesn't refer to the length of a Solar year (365.25 
days) or Lunar year (360 tithis, about 354.36 solar days) and is called a 
Savan year or the civil year. Nowadays it is not in use in any part of the world 
except for sacrificial purposes particularly for the Soma-yajna. 


2) In Surya Siddhanta, the Solar month is said to have 30.4382266 days 
(30. gh 26.17.37) and the Lunar month has 29.5305833 days (29. gh 31.50.6). 


|| The difference of 0.907643 days (gh 54.27.31) gets corrected by one inter- 


calary month after every 32 months and 15.246 days. For the pure Lunar 


|) year of about 340 days, the panchangs in India are corrected to be in line 


with the solar year by adding one adhika masa every 3 years or so. 


3) By taking a month of 30 days and a year of 360 days, one cannot go by the 
universally used Gregorian calendar. If the 360 day year rather than the 
365 day year is used for the mahadasa calculation, the gap between them 
would become more divergent with the dasa period, i.e. 6.25 days (365.25- 
360) after 1 year, 31.5 days (6.25x6) after 5 years, about 6 months after 
35 years, a whole year after 70 years, and a native may have to celebrate 
his 72 birthday even while he has yet to complete his 71st year under 
Vimshottari dasa of the 365 day year. 


4) The simplicity of calculation by dividing the year into months by multiply- 
ing by 12 and further converting into days by multiplying of 30 in the calcu- 
lation of the dasa balance at birth and sub sub (DBAS) dasa periods (in 
Brihat Parasara Hora Sastra, Phala Deepika, Tables of Bhukti and Anthara 
etc) cannot be understood as taking a 360 day year - 12 months x 30 days 
per month. The year is taken as 365.25 days. The actual dates computed by 
rigorous calculations by taking actual days of the months and by this simple 
method differ only by a few days; accurate practically for all astrological 
purposes. 


4. The KP astrologers and the vast, overwhelming majority of Vedic as- 
trologers, except some like Sadasiva Giri, Hira Gulrajani, N. Sundara Rajan, 
Rohini Ranjan, have used the regular solar year of 365 days. Since the 360 
day year dasa option is already incorporated in the SWs like KPAstro 3.0, 
JHora, the statistical study can be done easily to prove whether the 360 day 
year gives the better results. The bottom line is that one can use what works 
better for him as an individual astrologer, while simultaneously respecting 
the personal preferences of others.

KP for Beginners- Part 6 


Selection of Fruitful Significators 
Tin Win 





|.An event happens during the joint period of DBAS of the 
significators of houses under consideration. Many a time 
many planets and even all the 9 planets become the signifi- 
cators of the relevant house. In cases where the significators 
of the houses under consideration exceed more than four, 
the really beneficial or fruitful significators amongst them are 
to be found out after eliminating the unimportant significa- 
tors which are only tempters. This is really a very difficult 
task even for an experienced KP astrologer and most failures 
in prediction are mainly due to the wrong selection of fruitful 
significators. [he KP analysis starts from the cuspal sub lord 
for a matter that ends as an event with the help of fruitful sig- 
nificators. 


First Method 


2. The first method of selecting fruitful or beneficial significa- 
tors is to see the cuspal sub lord of the concerned houses, 
and to check which of the significators are posited in their 
stars. Those significators who are in the stars of such cuspal 
sub lords can be taken straightaway as fruitful significators. 
The rest can be dropped or eliminated by further consider- 
ation. 


3. The sub lord of the significator is the deciding factor re- 
garding the matters of the star lord and planet. If the sub 
lord is harmonious to the matters indicated by the star lord 
and planet, the significator gives favorable results. It is to take 
the planet which is posited in the sub of a significator whose 
star is not tenanted. If the sub lord is detrimental to the mat- 
ters indicated by the star lord and planet, the significator 
does not give favorable results. It is to take the planet which 
is posited in the sub of a significator whose star is not ten- 
anted. 


4. It is to find out whether a planet is a strong significator or 
a weak significator in the order in which one makes the se- 
lection of the significators. For example of marriage, if a 
planet is not at all connected with houses 2, 7, ||, except 
that one of the significators aspects it, then it is a weak planet. 
If the sub lord of a planet is a strong significator of the matter 
under consideration, then that planet is to be selected as a 
fruitful significator. But if the sub lord is one of the weak sig- 
nificators, then it is a weak planet. 


Second Method 


5. The second method is to select the fruitful significators 
with the help of the Ruling Planets (RPs) invented by Guruyji 
KSK. According to “The RPs at the time of query would be 
the RPs at the time of fructification of the event expected.”, 
the significators which are in common with the RPs are to 
be selected as the fruitful significators for the event in ques- 





Tin Win 
tw853@yahoo.com 


tion to get the correct result. 


6.In their order of preference or strength, the following plan- 
ets are called the RPs of the time when the chart is cast and 
judgment undertaken: 


I) Asc star lord 
2) Asc sign lord 
3) Moon star lord 
4) Moon sign lord 
5) Day lord 


7. The day is from sunrise to next sunrise. The RPs are to be 
taken at the time of query or judgment. Their help should be 
sought only when there is an urge to decide the significators 
which can bring out the event under consideration. The RP 
which is in the star or sub of a retrograde planet should be 
omitted and to take the remaining. 


8. If Rahu or Ketu is in conjunction or aspect with the RP or 
if it occupies the sign owned by the RP then Rahu and/or Ketu 
should be included in the RP. 


9. Some KP followers have added two more RPs of Asc sub 
lord and Moon sub lord. For the purpose of selecting the 
fruitful significators, the lesser number of RPs, i.e. the original 
5 seems more appropriate. 


10. Even here, it is to select such of those planes which are 
deposited in such a sub that contributes to the matter con- 
cerned. It is also to reject such a planet which happens to be 
both the significator of positive and negative houses, for ex- 
ample of marriage, the positive houses 2, 7 and | 1, and also 
the significator of the negative houses |2 to 2 or 7 or II, i.e., 
| or 6 or 10. If the dasa of such significator is running, in a few 
cases it may not give marriage; and so the next period alone 
may give marriage So that method of selection of fruitful sig- 
nificators is always useful. 


Third Method 


| 1. The third method of selecting fruitful significators is to 
check each significator whether its sub lord is included in the 
list of the significators. If yes, such a planet can be selected as 
a fruitful significators or else dropped. 


General Rules 


|2.As a general rule, all those significators which signify | 2th 
to the relevant houses under consideration should be re- 
jected. The planet whose sub lord is the significator of the 
house negating the house concerned i.e. in the | 2th to the 
house concerned should be rejected as an unfruitful significa- 
tor. The planets which are in 6,8,12 to the concerned house 
are supposed not to contribute to the matters signified by 
such houses. Similarly any house which is in 6, 8 and |2 to 


KP-Ezine September 2008 / 





any house are supposed to negate the matters governed by 
the house concerned. 


|3. Preference should be given to Rahu or Ketu, if it repre- 
sents any significator. A planet which appears many times 
amongst the significators/RPs or connected with various sig- 
nificators as their star or sign or as a sub lord should be se- 
lected as the strongest to give the result. Conversely a planet 
which is not in the sub lords of the concerned houses should 
be treated as the weakest in producing the result.

Bhava Cuspal Interlinks Through 


KB System 
Devara A 





A bhava cuspal (starting) point getting connection or inter- 
links with one or more other cuspal bhavas cuspal points, in 
the K.B. system, is called the “Bhavas interlinks’”. A bhava’s 
cuspal starting point is combined with the rasi lord, star lord, 
sub lord and sub sub lord etc, 


In the “Beginners stage Astrology” was defined the horo- 
scope response only the base of the Rasi lord. In the “Mid- 
dle stage astrology” was calculated the response with the 
bhava’s star lord. But the horoscope response are analyzed 
with the bhava’s sub lord method are called the “senior 
stage astrology’. 


Through the bhava’s sub sub lord, we can give the accuracy 
result of the horoscope is the “100% accuracy real position”. 
But the bhava sub sub lord position will change within a sec- 
onds. So, ordinarily it is so hard to use the sub sub position 
in the routine period. (Good mathematical knowledge is re- 
quired). 


Beginners stage Astrology: 


For example, in the olden days, if a birth took at the time of 
10.00 AM in a place and at that time the aries lagna is starting 
and upto 12.00 PM the aries lagna will stand. In this way the 
response will be common, if we tell about the rasi lord.. My 
humble opinion is, this prediction will be only 20%. 


Middle stage astrology: 


In this period, for example, the aries lagna starting at 10.00 
AM .Aswini 4 padhas, bharani 4 padhas and kiruthuigai first 
padhas are included in the aries rasi. The lagna will move upto 
10.50 in the aswini star, upto | 1.40 in the bharani star and 
upto 12.00 PM the lagna fall on the kiruthigai | padha. 


Same response will not happen within the 50 minutes be- 
cause in the mean time so many births will happen in the 
same town.All the birth can’t enjoy the same benefit among 
his life. But we can give the 40% result, with the help of bhava 
star lord, rasi karakam, bhava karakam and kala chakram. 


Senior stage astrology: 


Now a days, for example we take at 10.00 AM the aries lagna 
will starting. Upto 10.50 AM the lagna will move in the aswini 
(Kethu) star. The aswinin star was fabricated as a 9 divisions 
according the base of the kethu’s vimsothari dasa. Thus the 
births are identified and make differentiate within least min- 
utes. 


In the aries lagna, 000 to 00.46.40 degrees are in the kethu 
star and kethu sub lord. The lagna will move | degree within 
4 minutes. Here, the lagna will take the time nearly 3 minutes 
to move the 0.46.40 degree.

outer links’ and also called Mathi (Dasa-bhukthi) to the

riod.

The bhava cuspal inter links are sort out as 3 categories. 


These are; |. Equal reaction, 2. Independent reaction, 
3. Compound reaction. 


Equal reaction: 


If a planet, not to become a star lord or sub lord to the any 
bhava and a star lord of a planet also not to inter link with any 
other bhavas, such planets dasa-bhukthies periods, will not 
give notable kind of good or bad results to the any bhavas. 


But this planet in the star lord if it is positioned in a partic- 
ular bhava, sub lord of the planet may give a small level good 
or bad effect to the particular bhava. These inter links are not 
useful so much. 


Independent reaction: 


A planet is not positioned to any bhava’s sub lord. But that 
planet’s star lord and sub lord are inter linked with the other 
bhavas. Here, the sub lord act as a particular good or bad re- 
sponse to the star lord identified bhavas. 


The response will be come out as under explained, if a planet 
being as a bhava cuspal sub lord and a planet’s star lord and 
sub lord are inter linked with other bhavas. 


A planet sub lord gives good or bad results to the planet star 
lord inter linked bhavas and a planet inter linked bhavas. Par- 
ticularly, in the planet dasa bhukthi period, the Mathi goes 
along with the fate and give the fate response or result so 
strong. [hese reaction and response are come out repeatedly. 


Compound reaction: 


Just imagine, a planet may be many bhava’s cuspal sub lord 
and the star lord of the planet also being a many bhava’s cus- 
pal sub lord. 


Now, the planet’s sub lord react as a huge level with the 
planet's inter link bhavas and the planets star lord inter linked 
bhavas. 


Here, this planet being as many bhava’s sub lord and it is act 
as a fate of all the inter linked bhavas and this reaction will 
give a power to one’s life style to uplift or go downward. 


A person may get up-lift when the compound reactions in 
the permanent bhavas (1,2,6,7,10 bhavas) are connected to 
their 5,9,3,1 Ith bhavas. As well as,a person definitely come 
down from his life style, when the compound reactions in 
the permanent bhavas are connected to their 4,8,|2 bhavas 


So, the readers are advised to handle this mixture reaction 
rule very keen observation.

Evolution of KP from the KP original 


2 volumes to the KP Readers I-V 
Tin Win 





|. After having started reading the astrological books from 
July 1927, doing the research on the practical horoscopes 
from 1934, with the assistants from 1939, Guruji KSK found 
the method of the Krishnamurti Padhdhati in 1951 by Divine 
Grace and in 1958 he met Dr. B.V. Raman and explained his 
method. He published the first issue of the Astrology & 
Athrishta magazine on March 20, 1963, the Krishnamurti 
Padhdhati, 2 volumes in late 1966 by Sagar Publications and 
then the KP Readers | to VI in 1970-71 in his life time by Ma- 
habala Publishers, Hariman Publications. 


KP Reader I 


2. Almost the whole KP Reader | is taken from the Krishna- 
murti Padhdhati, Vol. |, 1966. The “Preface and Introduction, 
Ayanamsa-Verification (pp 61-74), To make use of Krishna- 
murti Epbhemerid and Casting of a Horoscope” and so on 
are added in the KP Reader I, 127-147. The “Table of Longi- 
tude and Latitude of various places (in India) (pp 68-92)”, 
‘Table showing the sub period of dasa” (pp I6I-173) and 
“Fortuna” (pp 471-474) in the the Krishnamurti Padhdhati, 
Vol. | are not included in the KP Reader I. 


KP Reader II 


3. The whole KP Reader Il is the reprint from the Krishna- 
murti Padhdhati, Vol. |, 1966, except the “Letters to the Au- 
thor and An Iterview with the Author” at the beginning of 
the book. 


KP Reader Ill of 1971 Original / Old Edition 


4. There are 2 parts, “Theoretical and Practical”, with sepa- 
rate paging. In the “Theoretical Part” of the KP Reader Ill, 
the contents in pp I-59 are taken from the Krishnamurti 
Padhdhati,Vol. | pp 475-533 and pp 60- 76 from the Krish- 
namurti Padhdhati,Vol.2 pp I-17; then in pp 77-108, it is the 
continued write up about Leo to Pisces lagnas as it was writ- 
ten up to Cancer lagna only in the Krishnamurti Padhdhati, 
Vol. 2. After that, the “Sub Useful for Detailed Reading” is 
added in pp 105-8. The contents in pp 108-130 are taken 
from pp 18-42 of the Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Vol. 2. The 
‘“‘Cusps and Subs- How to Judge” at the end of the “Theoret- 
ical Part’, pp 131-144, is added. It is Guruji KSK’s crowing 
part saying, “This discovery (of the sub-lord) has crowned 
me with success.” simultaneously appearing in the KP 
Reader V pp I31-144 and KP Reader VI pp 77-87, which was 
not included in the Krishnamurti Padhdhati, 2 Volumes. There 
is not any significant change in the Theoretical Part. 


5. Generally in the “Practical Part” of the KP Reader Ill, the 
contents in pp I-I07 are taken from the Krishnamurti Pad- 
hdhati, Vol .2 pp 43-169. But the “Theft and Chances of Re- 
covery” in pp | 16-122 of the Krishnamurti Padhdhati, Vol. 2

| |. Accordingly those earlier writings “to consider whether

Guest Arrival - a KP appraisal 
Vijay Kumar 





One of my important guest’s visit was overdue. | received a 
call on Thursday, 21-08-2006 from somebody else that the 
guest was reaching to me on Saturday (Aug 23, 2008). Out 
of curiosity, | thought to cross check it by KP and got moti- 
vated to analysis the arrival of the gust on Friday: Aug 22, 
2008 afternoon. 


The time chart was casted at Aug 22, 2008 at 16-27-34 Hrs 
IST’ at I2N51, 77E40.1 did rotate the chart to the I |h house 
for the guest, known to us. 


The rotated chart is presented herewith. 
Coordinates of judgment: 


¢ In the case of someone's arrival, primary function is the 
travel (3H), which the person has to undertake. Thus, 3rd 
cusp indicates the aspect of traveling. In case, if travel has to 
materialize to reach the destination, the 3rd cusp should have 
linkage to the I Ith house. 


¢ In case, if 3rd cusp is connected with the negative 
cusps/houses, the prospects of traveling get curtailed. 


The analysis of the chart: 
A brief snapshot of analysis is presented herewith. 
|. Examine Moon and Lagna 


Moon is a strong planet, as it does not have any planet in its 
star, hence its placement shall be important. Moon is placed 
in 6th house which being in 4th house from 6th house, makes 
it ill placed and thus cause obstructions to the travel.At the 
stellar level, Moon falls in the star of Venus placed in [Oth 
house in conjunction with the Sun who is the sub of Moon, 
thereby not indicating the prospects of travel. 


Looking at the disposition of the Moon, | was skeptical of 
the coming of the guest. | also noticed that Moon was the 
sub-lord of the 8th cusp, which confirmed my initial obser- 
vation. Thus, | did not find the guest having mental inclination 
for travel. 


Lagna owns Venus as the sub-lord.Venus falls in its own star 
and the placement of Venus in |0th house did not portend 
possibilities of his coming. Ketu as the sub-lord of Venus gets 
placed in 9th house, not connecting 3-| 1th houses. 


Interestingly, neither of Lagna and Moon find any connection 
with the 3rd house, thus the guest’s coming over to me was 
almost looking denied. 


2.Examine 3rd cusp 


It was pertinent to look at the 3rd cusp closely to see the 
possibilities of travel in particular. 


Jupiter lords the 3rd cusp as the sub-lord. While the retro-

gression of Jupiter is indicative of the delays and unforeseen 
negativities, its placement could be seen particularly as Jupiter 
is a strong planet because of having no planet in its star. Here, 
Jupiter is placed in 2nd house, which negated the 3rd house 
of travel and thus denied prospects of traveling. 


Looking from the stellar level, Jupiter falls in the star of Venus

more details. Rahu is a strong planet as not having any planet 
in its star, thus its linkage of 3rd cusp with the 3rd house by 
its own placement does indicate the desire of the guest for 
coming over to us. From the stellar level, Rahu falls in the star 
and sub of Mars and Mars’s placement in |0th house does 
not point to the traveling ultimately. If looked from the dispo- 
sition of Rahu through Saturn and Mars as well, no link of 3rd

From the above analysis, it was inferred that the travel of the 
guest might not materialize. 


3. Examine the | Ith cusp for final assessment 


| 1th cusp is Venus, and as analyzed in the preceding para- 
graphs, Venus does not link to the 3rd house. Thus, the travel 
of the guest was not destined. 


4. Examine the Dasha spread 


Venus-Sun-Moon was the dasha running at the time of 
prashna. Note that the antar-dasha lord was Moon and as an- 
alyzed in section #1, the prospects of traveling were not con- 
firmed al all. 


Thus, it was understood that the guest was not to travel and 
reach us. 


5. Facts of the case 


As indicated by the planetary configuration in the prashna 
chart, neither the guest reached us nor was any call to us.

riage rules are checked as under: 


|) 7 CSL Mo is in the dual sign Sg and it signifies 7,1 |. First rule is met.

2nd house as 2nd wife is not fulfilled as 2 CSL does not signify particularly 7 (legal bondage) and | 1.So 2nd mar- 
riage is not promised.

Expected Transfer - a KP appraisal 
Vijay Kumar 


ha 


One of my close relative, who is working at Mumbai was communicated about the proposal of his transfer to 
Bangalore and was asked to search the house at Bangalore for relocation, as the transfer case was in advanced 
stages of approval. Soon, | got the news and | tried to assess from KP if the native could be transferred from the 
job at Mumbai. 





With the question in mind “I want to know, if the native would be transferred to Bangalore’, | thought of a 
horary number |75 myself and prepared the chart on June 05, 2008 at | 7-37-28 Hrs at Bangalore. 


The rotated chart with respect to the | 1th house is presented as follows for analysis. 
Coordinates of judgment: 


¢ Essentially, a transfer in the same job to a different city location involves leaving the place of stay and get involved 
in the new environment. In pursuance to the above, the |0th house should get linked to 3rd and | 2th houses 
in order to account for leaving the place of stay and face a new environment. 

¢ In order to account for the change of place of stay, 4th cusp should link to the 3rd house. 

¢ | Ith cusp has the final say on the fructification of the query and should get linked with the relevant houses for 
achieving the results. Thus, for a change of place, the 4th cusp should get linked to the 3-| 1th house and for 
transfer to a new location; the |Oth cusp should get linked to 3-|2-1 1th houses. 


The analysis of the chart: 

A brief snapshot of analysis is presented herewith. 

|. Examine Moon and Lagna 

This is done to assess physical and mental status of the native. 

Note that the Lagna sub-lord is Moon, thus indications seen from Moon will be very pressing for the native. 


Moon is not a strong planet, as it has planets in its star, hence its placement is not of much importance. At the 
stellar level, Moon falls in the star of Rahu placed in 4th house, which indicates that the person does not have 
the mindset for a change of place. 


2. Examine 10th cusp 


|Oth cuspal sub-lord is Mars. Mars as 2-/th lord falls in the star of retro-Mercury as |2th lord placed in 8th 
house. The retrogression of star lord of |Oth sub-lord indicates some stagnation on job front and the placement 
in 8th house indicate some difficult scenarios on job front. 


Since, the star lord does not indicate the linkage of 3rd house, it does not call for any change of place. However, 
Mars falls in the sub of Venus, which as Asc lord finds its placement in 8th house. This clearly points the tough 
time, which the native must be facing on the job front (8th house) and his prestige (Asc lord) should have been 
at stake, though it is outside the scope of this prashna. 


Whatever be it, since the |0th cusp does not link to the 3rd house, thus the change of place had not been indi- 
cated through a job change. 


3. Examine the 4th cusp 
Analysis of 4th cusp would indicate, if the place of stay will get changed because of transfer. 


4th cuspal sub-lord is Rahu placed in 4th house. On stellar level, Rahu is placed in the star of Mars placed in | Oth 
house as 2-/th house lord. Rahu has Saturn as sub-lord, which again is placed in |0th house as 5th lord. 


Rahu is disposed by Saturn and Mars hence the significations of these planets may also be assessed. 


Saturn is a strong planet and is placed in |Oth house.At stellar level also, it disposes |O0th house without any link

Dictatorship-Equatorial Guinea 
As per KP Mundane View 


Kanak Bosmia 





= 


Short History: 


In 1968 Equatorial Guinea, until then an agriculturally based colony of Spain, won its independence,conducting it first Gen- 
eral Elections.. The nation immediately fell under dictatorship anda steep decline. President Obiang inherited a country 
that had lost two thirds of its population, where schools and churches had been closed, and the Central Government was 
in total bankruptcy. President Obiang and his new Government came into power in October 1979. 


Macias Nguema was elected as Equatorial Guinea's first President. However shortly after being elected, he abandoned dem- 
ocratic principles and declared himself Ruler-for-life in 1972. This was a dark and gloomy time for the nation. Macias 
Nguema ruled as a ruthless Dictator for | 1 years presiding over a regime that killed and tortured thousands of its own 
citizens. He died on September 29, 1979; Obiang was elected president on August 15, 1982 


The current president of Equatorial Guinea is Retired Brig. Gen. Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo.The | 982 constitution 
of Equatorial Guinea gives Obiang extensive powers, including naming and dismissing members of the Cabinet, making 
laws by decree, dissolving the Chamber of Representatives, negotiating and ratifying treaties and calling legislative elections. 
Obiang retains his role as Commander- in- Chief of the Armed Forces and Minister of Defence, and maintains a close su- 
pervision of military activities. The Prime Minister is appointed by the President and operates under powers designated 
by the President.The Prime Minister coordinates government activities in areas other than Foreign Affairs, National Defence 
and Security. 


On December | 5, 2002, Equatorial Guinea's four main opposition parties withdrew from the country's Presidential Election. 
Obiang won the election, widely considered fraudulent, by members of the Western Press. 

According to a March 2004 BBC profile, politics within the country are currently dominated by tensions between Obiang's 
son, Teodorin, and other close relatives with powerful positions in the security forces. The tension may be rooted in power- 
shift arising from the dramatic increase in oil production which has occurred since 1997.

Fate & Will 
Devaraj A 





When a person involves in an event (of any bhava), the gross quantum of results (either benefic or malefic) that 
can be accrued from that action is known as the ‘Fate’ (‘Vidhi’ in Tamil) of the individual in respect of that 
bhava. For any event, when the respective Fate of that bhava supports the particular action, the individual can 
get very benefic results in most of his life-time. 


On the contrary, if the Fate of that bhava doesn’t favour the same, the individual has to face malefic results in most 
of his life-time. Our fore-fathers have astrologically classified all the individual actions under the twelve bhavas. 
According to this classification, each bhava possesses many such significations within itself. 


As per the K.B SYSTEM, the starting points of bhavas known as bhava cusps are determining the 
Fate of the individuals. Because, these bhava cusps are observed uniquely in order to distinguish the results 
significantly for the births occuring even in very small intervals such as a minute, etc. The bhava cusps of twelve 
bhavas are considered as ‘Entry Gates’ for bhavas. Fate is being determined at these ‘Entry Gates’ of bhavas. 


A bhava cusp consists of the Bhava Lord, Star Lord and Sub-Lord. Among these, Star Lord is stronger than Bhava 
Lord and Sub-Lord is stronger than Star Lord. In short, Fate of a bhava is being determined mainly by the Sub- 
Lord of that bhava’s cusp. 


The Sub-Lord of any bhava is fully empowered to design the Fate, either as benefic or malefic results, in respect 
of that bhava by corresponding to other bhava cusps through its Star Lord (‘Saaram’) and Sub-Lord (‘Bhukthi’). 
Depending upon the strength of the basement only, we can decide the number of floors in any building. Similarly, 
Fate should be stronger enough for any bhava. 


Therefore, the actions of the individual are restricted to the extent of results determined by the Fate in respect 
of the respective bhava. The above explanation was made with an aim to make the readers understand that the 
individuals in their actions can not move an inch beyond the limits determined by the Fate. Let me explain this 
with an example. 


Let us consider a case wherein the Sub-Lord of | Oth bhava, links with 2nd, 6th and | 0th bhava cusps through its 
Star and Sub-Lord. As you know, the above 2nd, 6th and |O0th bhavas are promoting the welfare of | Oth bhava. 
Therefore, as the Fate of the individual in respect of | Oth bhava is good, we can conclude that the individual will 
do his profession in good manner in his life-time. 


On the contrary when the Sub-Lord of | Oth bhava linked with, Ist, 5th and 9th bhava cusps through its Star and 
Sub-Lord, the Fate of the |Oth bhava is considered very weak and thereby the individual will be forced to break 
the profession for a considerable period of his life-time. The reason is that the Ist, 5th and 9th bhavas are hap- 
pening respectively to be 4th, 8th and | 2th from the | Oth bhava. This indicates difficulties to the individual in his 
profession. 


An individual can execute those actions (of bhavas) hopefully for a long time, which (bhavas) are supported by 
the powerful Fate in his/her horoscope. Conversely, the individual either feels difficult to execute those actions 
(of bhavas) beyond a particular time or faces problems with regard to those bhavas, which are possessing week 
Fate in the natal horoscope. 


Particularly, the Fate of permanent bhavas viz. Ist, 2nd, 6th, 7th and |O0th bhavas should atleast be disposed with 
moderate strength. Because, these are the bhavas that are serving as sources of strength for human life. The 
chances are very remote to have all the bhavas with considerable strength of Fate. That is why, almost all the per- 
sons in the world are facing problems in one respect or another. So far, we have seen the basement of a horoscope 
namely ‘Fate’. Further, let us proceed to see Dasa-Bhukthi i.e. “Will? (Math? in Tamil). 


In confering the results, either good or bad, to the individuals for their actions during a particular period, the re- 
spective Dasa-Bhukthis (under the name Will) also taking a leading role, like Fate. Dasa-Bhukthis as Will are 
calculated based on the deposition of natal Moon. Dasa Lord is identified as the Lord of the Constellation, 


KP-Ezine October 2008 21 


Principles of KB System 


Fate & Will 
Devaraj A 





wherein the natal Moon deposited. Bhukthi Lord is ascertained by calculating the degree-wise extent of Moon’s 
traverse in that Constellation. 


A person’s horoscope is nothing but an astronomical record, wherein the Planetary and Bhava dispositions at the 
time of his/her birth are noted. Treating it as unchangeable, we call it as ‘Fate’ of the individual. But, as per the 
law of Universe, there is no such state as unchangeable. All the actions, depending upon the time-situation, are 
subjected to change according to the Divine Orders. 


Therefore, nothing is permanent /fixed in this Universe. The Dasa Bhukthi calculations, which are based on the 
disposition of Moon are impermanent. Similarly, our thought patterns also. Hence, in order to get accuracy in 
predictive astrology, the impermanent one (Will or Dasa Bhukthi) has to be synchronized with the permanent 
one (Fate). 


Dasa Bhukthis are building blocks of the predictive astrology. In my humble opinion, in the absence of Dasa 
Bhukthis Astrology is incomplete. As we know, the |2 bhava cusps are determining the Fate of the individual. 
But, all the incidents / actions denoted by Fate would not occur at a time in one lot. Dasa Bhukthis are executing 
those events in their turn at a particular time according to the bhavas they are relating to. 


In ascertaining the results of Dasa Bhukthis, K.B Astrology Method is specialist (individual) in nature. As per 
this method, effects of Dasa Bhukthis (Will) are sourced out from the Bhava cusps (Fate). That is “Will’ shall pro- 
ceed in the footsteps of ‘Fate’ and thereby execute its own duty. 


Therefore, a planet in its Dasa Lordship is empowered to execute certain actions / significations of those bhavas 
which are having this planet as Sub-Lord. Further, the Dasa (‘will’) will execute the results effectively to the 
extent of the ‘Fate’ determined by those bhavas. 


Nextly, the stellar disposition of the Dasa Lord should be taken note of. Because, the Dasa Lord is also empow- 
ered to undertake certain events / significations of those bhavas, which are having the bhava cusps corresponding 
to the Star Lord of this Dasa Lord. 


Nextly, the Sub-Lord of the Dasa Lord is determining the favourable / unfavourable results that can be expected 
from the bhavas for which bhava cusps are establishing links with Sub-Lord. The basis is as follows: For any bhava, 
the Ist, 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 9th and | Ith bhavas there from are promoting the bhava in question; the 4th, 8th, | Oth and 
|2th bhavas there from are denigrating the bhava in question; and 6th and /th bhavas there from is neutral in na- 
ture. 


In short, the Dasa Lord will confer the results of those bhavas, which are associated by the Dasa Lord, Star Lord 
of the Dasa Lord and Sub-Lord of the Dasa Lord.At the same time, the Fate of a bhava determined is restricted 
exclusively to that bhava alone. But, the Will, i.e. the effects of Dasa Bhukthis are not restricted to any particular 
bhava alone, instead they can exert influence on the other bhavas also as explained above. Let me explain this 
with an example. 


Let us assume that in a horoscope, Sub-Lord of Lagna bhava cusp is linked to 5th and 9th bhavas through its Star 
and Sub-Lord. During the above said Dasa of Lagna lord, as the 5th and 9th bhavas are promoting the Lagna bhava, 
‘Will’ proceeds on the path of ‘Fate’, and thereby very good health without any illness to the individual is ensured. 
At the same time, this Dasa Lord doesn’t fail to influence the other bhavas. When the 5th and 9th bhavas exert 
influence on the 2nd bhava, the individual has to face financial deficiency during this Dasa. Because, the 5thand 
9th bhavas are happening to be 4th and 8th bhavas respectively while reckoning from the 2nd bhava. Similarly, 
while exerting influence on the [Oth bhava (profession), severe set-back in profession is foreseen during this 
Dasa, as the 5th and 9th bhavas are 8th and | 2th bhavas respectively from the | Oth bhava. 


At the same time, as the 5th and 9th bhavas are in consonance with the promotion of other odd bhavas, during 
this Dasa the individual’s Lagna based karakas will be very good. But, as the 5th and 9th bhavas are supposed to 
denigrate all the even bhavas, the individual’s materialistic life itself suffered considerably during this Dasa. 

But, suppose the Sub-Lords of 2nd and |0th bhava cusps are corresponding (through their Star Lord and Sub- 
Lord) to the bhavas, which are favorable to 2nd and | Oth bhavas, then Fate in this respect may be considered as 
powerful. Then, the above said Dasa having connections with 5th and 9th are not fully empowered to destroy 
the 2nd and [0th bhava significations in its entire Dasa.

During this Dasa period, when the Bhukthi Lord is establishing connections with 4th and 8th bhavas, during that 
particular Bhukthi, Bhukthi Lord will overcome the Dasa Lord in promoting the individual with regard to his fi- 
nance (2nd) and profession (10th). Because, 4th and 8th bhavas are respectively |2th from the 5th and 9th 
bhavas. 


The 2nd and | 0th bhava significations will not be considerably affected till the Bhukthis of the planets having re- 
lationship with 3rd and 7th bhavas (being | 2th from 4th and 8th bhavas) are coming to operate. Even then, when 
the bhukthis of the planets having relationship with 2nd and 6th bhavas are operating, the Bhukthi Lord will over- 
come the Dasa Lord in conferring the results and prevent / resolve the problems, if any, with regard to his finance 
(2nd) and profession (| Oth). 


That is, ‘Fate’ is generalistic whereas, ‘Will (Dasa Bhukthis) is specialistic in nature. ‘Will’ can confer 
goodness to any particular bhava only to the extent of the ‘Fate’ determined for that bhava and thereby it can 
never overcome ‘Fate’. At the same time, it is noteworthy to observe that the Will (Dasa Bhukthis) is strong 
enough to exert influence on all the |2 bhavas. 


Therefore, general effects have to be determined by ‘Fate’ and individual effects known as time-specific events are 
ascertained by ‘Will’, i.e. Dasa-Bhukthis. Here, general effects are denoted by the actions (signified by the bhavas) 
of an individual, in which he engaged himself for a long-time either favorably or unfavorably. But, the individual 
effects (either favorable or unfavorable) represented by ‘Will’ are of short duration in his life-time. 


Even though a bhava is powerful by Fate, the actions / events denoted by that bhava can not be completed, in the 
absence of any support from the then operating Dasa-bhukthis of the individual. The prevailing Dasa-Bhukthis 
are fully empowered either to complete the action successfully or to put hold the event away from occurance. 
At the same time, even though the bhavas are weak by Fate, to some extent the operating Dasa-Bhukthis can pre- 
vent the evil effects signified by those weak bhavas during their period, provided the prevailing Dasa-Bhukthis are 
supposed to promote those events denoted by the corresponding bhavas. 


A good Dasa is like a quality vehicle to travel and the Bhukthis are like its pathway. While traveling in a good quality 
vehicle (good Dasa), even though the pathways (bad Bhukthis) are full of ups and downs, the destination can be 
reached safely by the vehicle (Dasa) by surpassing the hurdles. 


Conversely a bad Dasa is like a damaged vehicle and the Bhukthis are like its pathway. With the damaged vehicle 
(evil Dasa) the destination could never be reached, even though the pathways (Bhukthis) are very smooth. There- 
fore, when a Dasa failed to confer good results during its own sub-period (Bhukthi), we can con- 
clude that the Dasa is not at all good to that individual. Because, the Bhukthis are almost 
inoperative to overcome the Dasa in providing contradictory results. 


The Bhukthi lords are slightly empowered either to tone-up or to hold on the actions of the Dasa Lord, that too 
only in a feeble manner. Similarly, the Antara Lords (sub-sub-lords) will work depending upon the nature of the 
operating Bhukthis. In short, during the entire course of the Dasa, the effects of certain bhavas which are estab- 
lishing strong relationship with the Dasa Lord, can be frequently expected. 


A Dasa when favourably disposed of (by corresponding to good bhavas) in respect of the Ascendant-related sig- 
nifications (like health, education, conjugal relationships, etc.), the same Dasa should never be failed to denigrate 
the Ascendant-independant significations (like wealth, profession, property, etc.). Here, when the Ascendant-in- 
dependant significations are powerful by fate, the individual can reap some benefits during the relevant Bhukthis 
of the same Dasa by overcoming the Dasa Lord. 


That is, when a person involves in the actions of those bhavas which are not contravened by the Dasa-Bhukthis 
(‘Will’), the individual can reap very good results therefrom (the actions) and ultimately the bhava be promoted 
considerably. The chances for failure of the individual in those actions are very remote. Thus comes the famous 
saying of our ancestors, “Fate can be overcome by Will’. 


Next, let me tell in brief as how to utilize the concepts of ‘Dasa-Bhukthi-Anthra’ (Directions) in astrology. 
To understand the fixed issues (like longevity, health, finance, conjugal relations, etc.) the Dasa Lord should be as- 
sessed. Because, these fixed issues are applicable to all the people at all times. As the span of the Dasa is lengthier

Principles of KB System

than that of Bhukthi, Anthara, etc., the Dasa Lord will exert his considerable influence on the fixed issues in the 
entire Dasa. 


Similarly, the occurances which are happening in a few years (like marriage, constructing house and child birth, 
etc.) should be assessed from the Bhukthi Lords; the occurances which are happening in a few months or so (like 
recovering from disease, debt, unexpected happy or sorrow, etc.) should be assessed from the Anthara Lords; and 
the daily occurances should be assessed by assessing Sookshma Lords. 


Among these, Anthara will work according to the Bhukthi and Bhukthi will work in consonance with the Dasa. 
The Sookshma will work depending upon the Gochara (transits of planets). That is why our ancestors said that 
the predictions should be made by duly considering the Vidhi (Fate), Mathi (Will) and Gathi (Transits). But, some 
of our astrologers are used to consider Gochara (Transits of planets) with reference to the natal disposition of 
Moon, i.e. Rasi (Moon Sign) only. 


Even though they know pretty well that astrologically the total Signs (Moon Signs) in the Zodiac are just | 2, they 
are arriving predictions to the entire global mass of around 600 crore by classifying them as just |2 categories. 
In other words, they are making similar predictions for some 50 crore people of each category. According to my 
humble opinion, this is not only illogical but also unscientific. 


‘Will shall proceed on the pathway of ‘Fate’ in order to confer the results stored thereon in the form Fate. Ac- 
cording to K.B’s method of Astrology, as Gochara (transit) is determined with reference to the Bhava cusps as 
well as Directional influences in the form of Dasa-Bhukthis, the Gochara effects will be unique for each and every 
person and therefore even for the persons who took birth in the minutest time-difference of one minute or so, 
unique Gochara effects are determined. 


A horoscope is a store-house of all the informations regarding an individual’s birth to death. We, the astrologers 
could not predict all those informations in advance. The actions/happenings occuring in human life can be classified 
as two. First, the actions undertaken by ourselves frequently or for a long period of our life (fixed) and next, im- 
permanent happenings / incidents of our life. 


As astrologers, we can predict the results accurately only for fixed actions of human beings. Therefore, while mak- 
ing general predictions for an individual, we should consider the fixed issues only, for which the status of Dasa- 
Lord should be assessed with due weightage. 


Impermanent happenings / incidents of human beings has to be assessed only with reference to the situation and 
contemporary circumstances. Because, the time of occurence of such happenings / incidents are mainly deter- 
mined only with reference to the actions of the individual. Hence, when the individual is involving in an imper- 
manent action, the time of its fruition has to be delineated with reference to the then operating Bhukthis and 
Antaras. 


A person without taking any effort but putting forth to the astrologer a question, which is not at all related to 
his practical life-style, can very well be compared to asking a Doctor to predict the disease the individual would 
get after 10 years or so. 


For example, the effects of Dasa-Bhukthis of an individual, which corresponds to the 4th and | 0th bhavas would 
be as below. Fourth bhava denotes education, house, land, vehicle and production; and tenth bhava denotes pro- 
fession, fame and excessive production. During these Dasa-Bhukthis, the effects / significations exclusively of 
these two bhavas could not be expected. These 4th and | 0th bhavas will exert influence on other bhavas also and 
thereby confer good or bad effects to those bhavas. These 4th and | 0th bhavas denote: financial flow as these 
bhavas are 3rd and 9th from the 2nd bhava; increase in debt, disease and legal entanglements as these 
bhavas are | Ith and 5th from the 6th bhava; profession in competitive manner as these bhavas are /th and 
Ist from the 0th bhava. 


The 4th and [Oth bhavas are increasing the bhava karakas of the 2nd, 6th and |0th bhavas. It is certain that the 
above mentioned results are sure to happen during this period. But, suppose the requirement of the individual 
is child-birth, then the job of the astrologer would be simple, if the individual seeks to know whether he can get 
progeny during this Dasa-Bhukthi (4th and [0th) or not. As the 4th and |0th bhavas are 6th and | 2th bhavas

reckoning from the 5th bhava, it can be assessed that the chances for progeny during this Bhukthi are remote. 
But, during this Bhukthi, by delineating the period of Antharas which are corresponding to 3rd and 9th bhavas as 
favorable for progeny, we can guide the individual properly. 


Astrology possesses all the information of the universe in its mere |2 bhavas. Therefore, we should approach an 
astrologer with an open mind to discuss our problems in order to get proper guidance from the astrologer, as if 
approaching a doctor for our cure with free mind for counselling.

Will there be a switchover from Hotel Industry to Cine Field? 


On 19.01.2006, a new client came to my residence with a request to examine his horoscope. He said that he 
had been in the hotel industry since 20 years and had been incurring losses for a few recent years in the industry. 
Therefore, he has requested me to examine his horoscope astrologically as to continue in the hotel industry or 
to close it down. 


Further, he wished to know whether he could come out with flying colours in the field of acting in Cinema and 
Television, by quitting once for all the hotel industry. For the past two years, whenever chance arises, he used to 
act in small roles in Cinema and Television serials since he was very much interested in the field of Art, as reported 
by him. 


Now, let me share the views offered by me to my client after examining his horoscope. 
Before that let us see how the fate should be disposed of astrologically for undertaking the hotel business or art 
field as full time profession. 


Sixth bhava denotes Hotel Industry. That is, readers are well aware that the sixth bhava stands for food. In a horo- 
scope, when the sub-lord of the 6th bhava cusp linked 8th and | 2th bhava either from the 6th or from the 10th 
one cannot undertake hotel industry as his profession. 


But, when the 6th bhava cuspal sub-lord linked to its favorable bhavas viz. 2nd,4th,6th and |O0th bhavas .These 
bhavas are favorable to the | Oth bhava also. Then it implies that the fate has been favorably disposed of to un- 
dertake hotel business as profession. 


TheArt Field was represented by the 5th bhava. That is, the 5th bhava denotes the significations, which are giving 
pleasure to mind viz. prose, music and drama. Similarly, 7th bhava denotes audience or masses and 5th bhava is 
| Ith (pleasure) from 7th bhava. Therefore, it can be inferred that the professions, which are promoting mental 
pleasure and satisfaction to masses are all governed by the 5th bhava profession. 


Therefore, in a horoscope, when the sub-lord of the 5th bhava cusp linked to 8th and | 2th bhavas either from 
the 5th bhava (i.e.4th and |2th bhavas) or from the | 0th bhava (i.e. 5th and 9th bhavas), that person cannot shine 
in the field of Art long time . 


But, when the 5th bhava cusp sub-lord corresponds to its favorable bhavas viz. 2nd,3rd,6th,/th,!0th and I Ith 
bhavas both from the 5th bhava as well as from the | Oth bhava, then it implies that the fate has been favorably 
to shine well in the field of Art in long time. 


The above said approach appears to be complex / complicated to the readers. Generally, |Oth bhava stands for 
one’s profession. Similarly, each and every bhava have the karaka of |0th bhava. All the professions of the world 
are represented by the |O0th bhava under its ‘general karaka’. The specific professions denoted by particular 
bhavas are known under ‘special karaka’. According to that, the field of Art is represented by 5th bhava; Food, 
Dress and Health related fields are represented by 6th bhava; and House, Vehicle and Education related fields are 
represented by 4th bhava. 


The karakas of all the 12 bhavas piled up in any bhava have been narrated in detail in the book “‘Jothidathin 
Adippadai Thathuvam” (The basic principles of Astrology) written by my guru Prasanna Jothidamani 
K.Baskaran as well as in the book “K.B.Jothida Muraiyil Vidhiyum Mathiyum” (Fate and Will as per 
K.B.’s Method of Astrology) written by myself. By deep study of those books, readers can understand the 
bhava karakas in lucid manner. 


The |0th bhava determines a person’s deserved fate in respect of his general occupation /profession. When the 
sub-lord of the |Oth bhava cusp linked to its 8th and | 2th bhavas there from, the individual could not undertake 
any occupation / profession in good manner.

Saturn Dasa is in operation for the individual from 07.06.1997 to 07.06.2016. Dasa Lord Saturn is in the star of 
Venus and in the sub of Mercury. According to that, | wish to remember the readers once again, the Dasa Lord 
Saturn establishes cuspal links with the Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th bhavas. 


The above bhavas (Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th bhavas) are unfavorable both for the house of profession (10th bhava) 
as well the house of hotel industry (6th bhava). That is, these bhavas (Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th bhavas) include in 
themselves the 8th and | 2th bhavas reckoned from 6th and [Oth viz.|st, 5th and 9th bhavas. Hence, during the 
Saturn’s main period, the hotel industry has not prospered well. 


But, as the bhavas Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th, which are linked by the Dasa Lord, are favourable for the 5th bhava 
and as the Dasa Lord Saturn is in the Star of Venus, the main period of Saturn favors involvement of the individual 
in the field of Art. 


During the Saturn Dasa, Saturn Bhukthi, the individual could not run the hotel business smoothly. He incurred 
heavy losses. But, during the same period, he got some opportunities to act in a few serials of small screen. This 
continues up to the Mercury Bhukthi. 


It is to be noted here that in the Saturn and Mercury Bhukthis of Saturn Dasa, the individual has not shown 
proper interest in his hotel business. In the Ketu Bhukthi, which followed the Mercury Bhukthi, he did not get 
chances for acting in the field of Art. He ignored the few opportunities in the Television channels and searched 
for chances in Cine field. In the Ketu Bhukthi, he could not get it. But, he observed some improvements in his 
hotel business during this ketu period. 


Because, Ketu is in the star of Jupiter and in the sub of Moon. Ketu is the Sub-Lord of | Ith bhava cusp. Jupiter 
is the Sub-Lord of 2nd, 4th and 6th bhava cusps. Moon, by strongly establishing relationships with 2nd, 6th and 
|Oth bhavas improved the 6th bhava prospects (the hotel industry). But, as the 2nd, 4th, 6th and | Oth bhavas are 
not supporting to the 5th bhava, the chances of acting has been reduced considerably during the Ketu Bhukthi 
of Saturn Dasa (i.e. from 18.02.2003 to 28.03.2004). 


The next Venus Bhukthi, which follows Ketu Bhukthi was favourable for the 5th bhava prospects. Already we have 
seen that the links established by the Venus are Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th bhavas. As these cuspal links are detri- 
mental (unfavorable) to the 6th bhava, the hotel business was affected severely during Venus Bhukthi of Saturn 
Dasa (i.e. from 28.03.2004 to 29.05.2007). 


As Venus is the Sub-Lord of the 5th bhava cusp, the ‘Fate’ stored for the individual for 5th bhava will be executed 
as ‘Will’ of the individual and thereby thrive the native towards Art field. Further, as Venus is the Sub-Lord of as- 
cendant also, his thought patterns and characteristics will be based on Ist, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th bhavas. Then, let 
us see how he was in the hotel industry for 20 years and above. 


When the individual was undergone Jupiter Dasa, the hotel business was running successful. Because, Jupiter is 
the Sub-Lord of the 2nd, 4th and 6th bhava cusps. Jupiter is in the star of Ketu and in the Sub of Saturn. Ketu is 
the Sub-Lord of | 1th bhava cusp and Saturn is the Sub-Lord of the | 0th bhava cusp. Therefore, Jupiter establishes 
strong cuspal links with the 2nd, 4th and 6th bhavas. 


Further, being the Sub-Lord of the 6th bhava, Jupiter executed the results of 6th bhava fully. In this horoscope, 
even though the fate in respect of occupation, i.e. |Oth bhava (Saturn) is not well-disposed, the planets which are 
in the star of Saturn (here Jupiter and Mercury are in the star of Saturn) will execute the results of |Oth bhava 
according to their cuspal links. 


Accordingly, Jupiter by being the Sub-Lord of the 2nd, 4th and 6th bhava cusps and thereby strengthens the bhavas
